name: AAUW Madtown 5K
description: The race begins at 8 am Cedar Creek at 500 N Westberry in Madera, California. The runners will run north on Westberry and then turn left on Riverview until you come to an entrance to run along the cannel. You will turn around at the marked area and return to Cedar Creek where we will have breakfast and provide the runners with their times. Each runner will be provided with a T-shirt.

name: Abrazo 5K Walk & 10K Run 2026
description:
Abrazo 5K Walk & 10K Run

This year’s Abrazo 5K Walk and 10K Run embraces the theme “Get Up, Stand Up.” Inspired by Bob Marley’s words, “One love, one heart, let’s get together and feel all right,” we honor his legacy of using music to uplift voices, champion social justice, and spread messages of love, unity, and resilience.

Casa Familiar continues this spirit through our mission of Advancing Communities—even in the face of adversity—by celebrating the strength of our comunidad.

Join us to uplift community wins and support Casa’s youth and senior programs. As a participant, you’ll help us meet growing needs while celebrating together.

Expect lively Rasta vibes, energizing music, and two special awards presented after the race during a short closing program.

Event Details

The Abrazo 5K Walk & 10K Run takes participants along the scenic San Ysidro–Tijuana border. This year, we’re excited to bring back the Beer Garden — celebrate after the run with a refreshing drink! Beer access is included with your food and drink bracelet.

Welcoming more than 300 participants each year, this annual fundraising event is packed with community spirit, fun, and contagious energy.

Date:

Saturday, May 2, 2026

Schedule:

  • 6:30 AM: Registration 

  • 7:00 AM: Welcome 

  • 7:30 AM: 10K Run

  • 7:35 AM: 5K Walk 

  • 8:45 AM - 11 AM: Awards & Raffles

name: Abrazo 5K Walk & 10K Run 2026
description:
Abrazo 5K Walk & 10K Run

This year’s Abrazo 5K Walk and 10K Run embraces the theme “Get Up, Stand Up.” Inspired by Bob Marley’s words, “One love, one heart, let’s get together and feel all right,” we honor his legacy of using music to uplift voices, champion social justice, and spread messages of love, unity, and resilience.

Casa Familiar continues this spirit through our mission of Advancing Communities—even in the face of adversity—by celebrating the strength of our comunidad.

Join us to uplift community wins and support Casa’s youth and senior programs. As a participant, you’ll help us meet growing needs while celebrating together.

Expect lively Rasta vibes, energizing music, and two special awards presented after the race during a short closing program.

Event Details

The Abrazo 5K Walk & 10K Run takes participants along the scenic San Ysidro–Tijuana border. This year, we’re excited to bring back the Beer Garden — celebrate after the run with a refreshing drink! Beer access is included with your food and drink bracelet.

Welcoming more than 300 participants each year, this annual fundraising event is packed with community spirit, fun, and contagious energy.

name: Akash Wine Run 5k
description:
THIS RACE WILL SELL OUT SOON SO SECURE YOUR SPOT TODAY!

Like Running or Walking?  Love Wine?  This race is for you! 

Join us on Sunday, March 1, 2026 at 10:00am for an exciting annual event that features Akash Winery & Vineyards. Come join us on the gorgeous, open-air patio, where you’ll find far more than beautiful views and amazing wine. This winery is loved by locals and out-of-towners alike, thanks to the happy energy and friendly faces of our knowledgeable team.  So, whether you are looking to run, walk or just enjoy the wine and camaraderie this race is a sure thing for a great time and an incredible experience! This race is timed and scored by J3 Timing.  Results will be posted at www.J3Timing.com. 

Registration Includes:

  • T-shirt:  Super Soft Ring Spun Cotton t-shirt included! 
  • Wine Glass: Shatterproof, Collapsible, and Portable!
  • Finisher Medal: Doubles as a Wine Stopper!
  • Race Bib: Chip timed 5k run/walk
  • Results Posted Online
  • ...and of course, a pour of wine!

name: Alameda Island Running Festival
description:
We are back for another year of racing with our start and end at Faction Brewery. The race start and finish will be right outside, and the Health and Wellness expo presented by Alameda Health Systems will be inside the old hanger.
As with all of our events, a portion of our registrations will be donated to our Beneficiary Alameda Education Foundation. you can read more about them from our direct links below:
  • Alameda Education Foundation: https://alamedaeducationfoundation.org/
 
Race Weekend Packet Pick Up:
  • Thursday and Friday September 17th and 18th : Lauren's Closet 1420 Park St, Alameda, Ca. 94501
    • 10:00am - 6:00pm * we encourage you to get your BIB and shirt early and sleep in race morning! 
  • Saturday 1:00pm - 5:00pm Race Start/Finish Expo 2501 Monarch St, Alameda Point - Faction Brewery
  • Sunday: 6:30am - 8:15am Race Start/Finish Expo 2501 Monarch St. Alameda Point - Faction Brewery
 
Race Events and Schedule: 
  • Saturday: 
    • Hella Bae Running 5k and 1 Mile Shake-out run presented by Skechers : 1:00pm
    • Yoga in the Hanger presented by Breathing Room Studio
  • Sunday 
    • Half Marathon: 7:30am
    • 10K: 8:00am 
    • 5k Presented by Penumbra: 8:15am
    • Family Fun Run: 10:00am
 
Race Timing and Restrictions:

the Island Running Festival is a chip-timed event.  Participants can run, jog or walk the entire course. 
Jogging strollers are permitted but are asked to start in the back of the pack.  Wheelchair athletes are permitted but due to safety concerns and street closure restrictions cannot travel faster than the fastest runner.   No bikes, scooters, skateboards or other wheeled vehicles are allowed. Dogs are not allowed on our race courses.  We love dogs, but there are those who are not so comfortable around them and there are also dogs that are uncomfortable around hundreds of other people, therefore NO DOGS ALLOWED on the course or at the finish line.

We will provide bike parking for those of you that prefer to bike to the event. See the race website for more details. 

 
Event info:
For more detail about the individual events our website

 

Medical and Water Stops:

We will have a dedicated paramedics team on site and available to help assess your race day medical needs and administer acute first aid when necessary. A medical station will be located near the finish line and team members will be roaming the course. 
Water Stops: see maps page for more info
  • Half: Mile 2, 5.5 & 11
  • 10k: Mile 2, 5.5
  • 5k: Mile  2 & 2.5 
 
Volunteers:
We can always use volunteers and it takes the support or our community and friends to make these events successful. if you are interested in learning more visit our website and volunteer support page or reach out to info@outfrontendurance.com

name: Alameda July 4th Parade R.A.C.E.
description:
Come out for our July 4th tradition and run this flat and fast point to point 5k thru the closed streets of Alameda. We will be starting again at 8:30am to provide ample space between our runners and the Parade that follows. 

General Overview: 

The 5K run (3.1 mile) and walk takes you through beautiful Alameda winding thru business and residential streets. This run benefits the Midway Shelter of Alameda. 

Packet Pick-up:

  • 7/1 thru 7/3: Laurens Closet. 1420 Park St, Alameda. Hours 10:00am - 5:00pm  
  • 7/4 Race morning registration opens at 7:30am 1440 Park St, Alameda ~ La Pena corner of Santa Clara (New Location)

Race Day Details: 

  • Start: 1420 Park St. Alameda, ca. 94501
  • Packet Pick-up : 7:30am
  • Race Start : 8:30am
  • Finish: 1526 Webster St, Alameda, CA 94501 (across from Tapout Fitness)

We will have shuttle service in 2026 to get runners back to the start. We have made strides towards this for a couple years and we finally have it lined up for this year. 

 

If you are traveling via Bart or public transportation please review the schedules below to get you to the race start, and picked up from the race finish. 

  • Bart Website: https://www.bart.gov/
  • AC Transit Site: https://www.actransit.org/

name: Alien Run – 5K, 10K, 10M, and Half Marathon
description:
The Alien Run is landing just in time for an epic UFO Day celebration! Get ready to run, walk, or teleport your way through a course filled with cosmic energy, mysterious encounters, and out-of-this-world fun. Whether you're racing across galaxies or just cruising under the stars, this adventure is your chance to celebrate the wonders of the universe — and maybe spot a few visitors from beyond! Suit up, power up, and let's make some extraterrestrial memories!

Race Details

Start Location: Long Beach Location TBD
Parking: Parking in the lot is $2/hour and starts at 8am, if you are running the Half/10m you can use the Passport app to pay for parking. Street parking is free.

Event Schedule

6:20am – Bib pick-up opens at the tables closest to Claremont Ave
7:00am – Half marathon & 10m start
7:30am – 5k & 10k start
7:35am – Registration & start line close
10:20am – Course closes (3 hours, 20 minutes for the Half and 10m)

Early start of 6:30am may be pre-arranged for half marathoners, email your request to events@hightideruns.com. All early starters will not be eligible for awards.

Out and Back Course

5k & 10k: The 5k route is used for the 5k (one lap) and 10k (two laps) – 5k route
10m: The 5m route is used for the 10m (two laps) – 5m route
Half: The 5m route is run twice and the 5k route is run once for the Half – 5m route and 5k route

More about the Course

The beach path is an open course, so you will encounter others using it. When we start the race, please stay on the right side of the beach path. The right side is for pedestrians and the left side is for cyclists.

On-Course Support: A fully stocked water station is located at the Belmont Pier. The finish line will also have an aid station stocked with water, gatorade, gels, and fruit snacks. We have a first aid kit at each station and all High Tides Crew Members have received CPR training. The turns are clearly marked with chalk, a runner turn sign, and a flag

Final Details

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!
Gear Check: You may leave personal items with staff at the registration tent. Please bring your own bag.
Awards: 1st place medals are given to the overall 1st male and female in each distance.
Results & Photos: An email with race results and photos will be sent the day after the race and earlier on Instagram. Race photos are free!

Join Us Again: Did you have a blast running with us at our low-pressure, high vibes race? We have themed races throughout the year in Long Beach, Santa Monica, the San Fernando Valley, and Orange County. Register for multiple races at a time to earn a discount. Check our full schedule

Have Another Question? Check our FAQ page, it's probably answered there!

name: Almond Blossom Run 2026
description:
Welcome to the 2026 Almond Blossom Run!!


Durham Sports Boosters is excited to announce that the 44th annual Almond Blossom Run will be held Sunday, February 22, 2026!

Please join us in Durham for a beautiful Sunday morning run around the almond orchards with the trees in full bloom to see how special this race really is! As in past years, this event will include a 5K and 10K run with chip timing provided by Under the Sun Events. 

For our 2026 race, you have three options to enjoy our event:

  • A live, in-person event with waves every 5 minutes based on your registration level
  • A virtual event on our official course at your convenience-if you would like to enter the results for your run, please do so the morning of the Feb. 22nd by 9AM
  • A virtual, make-your-own course-if you would like to enter the results for your run, please do so the morning of the Feb. 22nd by 9AM


In-person participants (with data submitted via RunJoy, etc.) are eligible for top male and female finisher awards. Winners in both the 5K and 10K events will receive a gift certificate for a pair of running shoes from Fleet Feet in Chico. Medals will be awarded to the top finishers for each age division as well. Register here now!

Participants in the virtual event will receive instructions on how to submit virtual times, but will not be eligible for prizes.

Registration for in-person and virtual race is just $45 (with $1.85 convenience fee). Participants may choose from a long-sleeved, technical or short-sleeved, poly-cotton blend shirt upon registration, but be sure to register early-limited sizes and styles have been pre-ordered, so be sure to register early. Please note: For those participating in the virtual make-your-own course race, there will be a $10 shipping fee for those wanting a shirt.  

Sponsors are a critical partner in this event and allow us to continue our financial support of our athletic programs in Durham. Proceeds from the 2026 run will benefit student athletic teams at both Durham Intermediate School and Durham High School. Durham Sports Boosters is currently seeking funds to update the scoreboard and PA systems and the DHS Coliseum, upgrade equipment for boys and girls teams at both DHS and DIS, and implement improvements to the high school gym trophy cases. Thanks to our racers and generous sponsors, over $35,000 was spent in 2025 on our many athletic programs. We were able to purchase updated uniforms for DHS Cheer, Volleyball, Ski/Snowboard, and DIS basketball, equipment for Softball, Golf, Track and Field, and the Swim Team. Durham Sports Boosters also collaborated with Durham Park & Recreation to update the pool cover, and with the Durham Gala and Durham Volunteer Firefighters to purchase two new scoreboards for the DHS Gym. We have been busy, and it is because of supporters like you! Please click the donation tab here to see how you can support our athletes. 

You can become a part of our 2026 sponsorship team for this great event through this registration portal for as low as $100. In addition to knowing you have supported a great cause for our athletes, you will also receive wonderful advertising for your company. The race is on!

name: Almond Bowl 5K & 10K November 1st, 2026
description:
Join us, in person, on November 1st, 2026 for the 52nd Annual Almond Bowl in the beautiful Lower Bidwell Park!

Keeping with the Chico tradition we will be hosting a 5k and 10k race starting on South Park Drive and finishing near the Sycamore Field. The price of this race includes your race shirt from Upper Park Clothing, a race bib for you to wear during your run and plenty of post-race snacks for after your run! 


This race, along with the Bidwell classic, are fundraisers for our local high school's cross-country teams and band programs! Additional donations can be accepted in the registration page! 

 

RACE START TIMES


5k: 8:00am

10k: 8:10am

 

REGISTRATION

Registration for this year's Almond Bowl will be available online. In person registration will be available during packet pick up only. 

 

Race Fee Schedule

Dec 11th - March 31st - (online)              10k $50.00

                                                                        5k $40.00

April. 1st - August. 31st - (online)           10k $55.00

                                                                        5k $45.00

September 1st - Oct. 30th                        10k $60.00

(online @ 9am)                                             5k $50.00

In person Registration at Packet Pickup 
 
                                                                      10k $60.00

                                                                        5k $50.00
 

In person registration will be available at Fleet Feet Chico during packet pickup ONLY. (October 30th and 31st, 2026) Packet pickup will be from 10:00am - 2:00pm Friday and 9:00am - 2:00pm on Saturday. 

 
Registration Information
Online registration closes October 30th at 9:00 a.m. Registration will be available in person on October 30th and 31st at Fleet Feet Chico from 10am-2pm on Friday and 9am-2pm on Saturday. You need to Register by Friday October 16th to guarantee yourself race shirt. If you register between October 16th - November 1st your shirt will NOT be guaranteed. Limited number of extra shirts will be available first come first serve at packet pickup. All left over shirts/unclaimed shirts will be available for pickup or for sale (non-registered runners) AFTER the race on November 1st. Shirts will be first come first serve starting at 9:00am.  

OFFICAL COURSE CERTIFICATION AND MAPS

5K and 10K: Flat, fast loop through beautiful (newly paved!) lower Bidwell Park. 

Click here for both course maps.

 

DIRECTIONS AND PARKING FOR OPTIONAL RACE LOCATION

To the course:
Enter Chico via Highway 99 either from the north or from the south. If you are coming from the north on 99, take the Highway 32 offramp and turn right at the first intersection. If you are coming from the south on 99, take the Highway 32 offramp and turn left at the second intersection. Now you're heading west on 32 (East 8th St). From here. If coming from north 99 take the highway 32 exit and turn right onto 8th St. 

Take 8th St just under a half-mile, then turn right on Sycamore St.
Sycamore St runs a few blocks into Woodland Ave, which runs parallel to the park. The park itself will be closed to vehicle traffic on race day, so find a parking spot on or near Woodland Ave. Please be courteous and park legally. Do not park in a way that blocks local residents' entry to or exit from their homes.
There are several entrances to the One Mile Recreation Area from Woodland Ave. For race-day packet pickup, look for the sign marked pre-Registered. For any other assistance, make your way to the Information booth.


 

PACKET PICKUP

Packet pickup will be held at Fleet Feet Chico on the following days and times:

Friday and Saturday October 30th and 31st, 2026

10:00am-2:00pm (Friday)

9:00am-2:00pm (Saturday)

Fleet Feet - Chico
241 Main Street
Chico, CA 95928
(530) 345-1000

 
Race Rules:
Be courteous when overtaking slower runners or walkers in your elected race location. We want you to race hard and fast, but with safety of yourself and others in mind.

Where your Race number so it is visible on the participant's front!

Run your race with pride!

You must cross the timing mat for your chip to be read. If you are planning of racing for top finisher, the race is based on gun time and first to cross the finish line.

All other placements (age groups) will be based on chip timing.


Run, hard, run fast and have fun!


No pets will be allowed on course during the race.


All strollers must start at the back of the pack.


Thank you for understanding. 
 

AID STATIONS AND RESTROOMS
There will be 3 for the 10k and 2 for the 5k.

1.     Cedar Grove Bathrooms – Water 
2.     Peterson Drive Gate – Water 
3.     99 Overpass (Vallombrosa side) – Water
Restroom on the course will be located at One Mile recreation on the North and South side of the pool, Cedar Grove Park, and Pettersen Dr. Park entrance as well as portable restrooms at the start and finish.
 
 

T-SHIRTS AND AWARDS
Guaranteed Tee-shirt cutoff is October 16th, 2026

Cotton Poly blend shirts from Upper Park Clothing Co. will be provided to all participants who register for this event before the tee shirt cutoff. (10/16/26) Any participant who registers on or before October 16th will be guaranteed a race tee. Any participant who registers after October 17th will be able to receive a race shirt based on a limited size availability (very few extras will be ordered). Any shirts not picked up at packet pick up prior to the race will be available on a first come first serve basis to all paid runners for pick up, and available for sale to any unregistered spectators starting at 9:00am at the Fleet Feet booth. 
All shirts come in adult male (unisex) sizes, so you may wish to choose a smaller size than normal for female and child runners. No youth sizes will be available. 
 

AWARDS FOR TOP FINISHERS
 
We will be offering a CASH PRIZE Top male and female for each race! (5k & 10k) We will have an award ceremony at 8:30am for the 5k, 9:00am for the 10k.
 
Age group awards can be found at the Fleet Feet tent following the award ceremony for each race. 
(Awards will also be offered to the top three in each age group category for each gender in each race)
 
All unclaimed prized will be available for pick up at Fleet Feet Chico on Tuesday 3rd during regular business hours. (10:00am-5:00pm)

Age group brackets will be as followed: 

14 and under / 15-19 / 20-29 / 30-39 / 40-49 / 50-59 / 60-69 / 70 and over
  
For more information, please email kristina@fleetfeetchico.com or shawna@feetfeetchico.com

**No Refunds on race entries or merchandise purchased for this event**

name: Always Hope Easter Run 5K/10K/13.1 LOS ANGELES
description:
🐣 Get ready to lace up your sneakers and chase some fun!
Join us for the Always Hope Easter Run - a family-friendly, fun, and make memories that’ll last longer than chocolate eggs!

 

Overview:
Run will sell-out QUICK! We will close off waves the moment they fill up. If waves are sold out, you can sign-up for the virtual run option or wait list.
This is a smaller, private group run with a cap per wave.
All paces and ages (under 18 with guardian) are welcome - Run or Walk!  
There's no equipment or setup, this is a pure run with our coordinators to support you in a warm, stress-free setting!
When you sign-up, we give you the support you need to help you achieve your goals and fitness. We also invite you to be part of our local run clubs that supports your fitness journey. 
Timing:
- Timing is Optional: You may track your time on an app (Strava, RunKeeper, Nike Run, etc) and submit your times with our easy form to be posted online. Or you can ask our coordinators to help keep track of your time. 
- No timing chips (This is a stress free run to support you in achieving your goals)!
What You Get (Swag Bag):
- Running T-Shirt (Shipped to the address you register with - US only)
- Finisher's Towel or Giveaway
- Finisher's Medal! 
- Digital Training Pack 
- Online Results & Certificate of Completion
- Invitation to Join one of our Local Running Clubs
- We now have Technical Running Shirts (Optional). These lightweight, moisture wicking shirts can be upgraded for just $5 more. 
Packet Pickup:
No hassle of picking up packets required!
-Swag shipped direct to your address (Please make sure you provide your full, correct US mailing address including apartment number and check spelling)
- Race bibs are provided on race day
When will I get my Swag?
You will get your shirt at your mailing address the week of your race.
Race Updates:

name: Anaheim Ducks 5K presented by Arrowhead Water
description:
The 4th annual Anaheim Ducks 5K presented by Arrowhead Water is coming back to Great Park in Irvine on Sunday, February 8th!

The course will start right outside of the Ducks practice facility - Great Park Ice & FivePoint Arena - and proceed throughout and around the park.

This year's event will include appearances by Anaheim Ducks mascot Wild Wing, a vendor village with family friendly games and activities, music by DJ JoJo, and much more. All proceeds will benefit the Anaheim Ducks Foundation's mission of producing positive change for children and families throughout Southern California by providing educational opportunities, broadening access to the sport of hockey and addressing the health and wellness needs of the community.

Both competitive and casual runners/walkers are welcome, and each participant will receive a race day t-shirt, finisher's medal, and souvenir runner's bib. Plus - attendees who register for the 'DUCKS 5K + Game Ticket!' option during registration will also receive (1) Terrace Level ticket to a Ducks home game at Honda Center!

name: Anaheim Turkey Trot 5K/10K  -Corner of Katella on the SANTA ANA RIVER TRAIL.  Across the street from Honda Center
description:
Anaheim Santa Ana River Trail Turkey Trot 5K/10K
Run up a Thanksgiving appetite at this year’s Anaheim Santa Ana River Trail Turkey Trot! Caren Ware Events brings you the ultimate race bling and the best holiday-themed motivation to stay healthy and active. Enjoy a scenic run along the paved Santa Ana River Trail and finish with a view of the iconic “Big A” of Angel Stadium.

Event Location:
Just north of Katella & S Douglas Road on the Santa Ana River Trail, between Angel Stadium and the Honda Center.
Closest Google address: 2610 E. Katella Ave, Anaheim, CA 92806 (former JT Schmid location).

 
What Each Participant Receives:
A collectible themed turkey shirt, beanie, or stuffed event turkey
A custom cast Turkey finisher medal or a choice of race beanie
Chip timing by ITZABOUTTIME with age division awards (3-deep per 5-year span)
A fresh slice of pumpkin pie with whipped cream at the finish
Fun, camaraderie, and holiday cheer
Enjoy music, a festive “along the fence” event expo, Thanksgiving decorations, and photo ops!

 
Race Day Schedule:
6:30 – 8:00 AM: Registration & walk-up packet pick-up
7:50 AM: Warm-up session
7:55 – 8:10 AM: Rolling start for 5K & 10K (must start by 8:10 AM)
8:11 AM: 1-Mile Fun Run start
9:00 AM: 5K Awards Ceremony (top overall & age divisions)
9:30 AM: 10K Awards Ceremony
All participants must wear the correct bib on the front for proper scoring.

 
Early Packet Pickup 

Pickup Details:

TBD

You may pick up packets for others; no ID required.

Race Day Pickup: 6:30 AM at registration booth near start/finish

 
Course Information:
Location: Santa Ana River Trail, Anaheim (paved, multi-use trail)
Enjoy views of Angel Stadium along the way
Shared path with cyclists, walkers, and dog walkers
Safety: Stay right, allow space for others, and follow public path rules
Pro tip: Write what you’re thankful for on your race bib!
 
Parking Information:
Designated Event Parking: Angel Stadium back lot (adjacent to Transit Center) – $10 race day cash pay to attendant or make payment  via zelle carenfasttrack@aol.com or venmo caren-Ware-1 have proof to show attendants. Or prepay when registering.

name: Anime Fan and Fitness Festival
description:
Initial Mile proudly presents to you Anime Fan and Fitness Festival, the festival where anime and fitness collide.

Join us for our second annual Anime Fan and Fitness Festival in Gilroy, CA on Saturday, September 19, 2026! This year we are leveling up. We are not only excited to bring back our 5k run event, but are also excited to announce our new experiences, the Little Ninja Dash and our new 5k Hybrid Quest. 

Our new and unique race, 5k Hybrid Quest will take warriors on a journey to become the warrior of their universe as they won't only run the course, but will step fully into their story as they face a series of physical and mental challenges inspired by the anime universe before making their triumphant return to Victory Village.

Whether you’re a seasoned runner, a casual jogger, a dedicated fitness enthusiast, a creative cosplayer, or a passionate anime fan, this event was made just for you. All experience levels are encouraged so gather your friends, family, lace up your shoes, and step into a world where miles meet manga as we bring anime energy to every stride. Cosplay is highly encouraged, so suit up as your favorite character and make this run a true celebration of anime culture! 

Register today and become the warrior of your universe!

name: Artesa Wine Run 5k
description:
Like Running or Walking?  Love Wine?  This race is for you! 

Join us on Sunday, March 8, 2026 with start times at 8:30am or 10:30am (you will select your start time during registration) for an exciting annual event that features Artesa Vineyards Winery. Escape to Artesa Winery, just an hour from San Francisco, and enjoy the finest high-end wines, explore Spanish-inspired architecture, and savor tapas that perfectly complement our exceptional selection. Whether you are looking to run, walk or just enjoy the wonderful wine and camaraderie this race is a sure thing for a great time and an incredible experience!  This race is timed and scored by J3 Timing.  Results will be posted at www.J3Timing.com. 

Registration Includes:

  • T-shirt:  Super Soft Ring Spun Cotton t-shirt included! 
  • Wine Glass: Shatterproof, Collapsible, and Portable!
  • Finisher Medal: Doubles as a Wine Stopper!
  • Race Bib: Chip timed 5k run/walk
  • Results Posted Online
  • ...and of course, a pour of wine!*

name: Ascot Hills Challenge 5K
description:
Event proceeds benefit Wilson High School Fire and Police Magnet Cadet Program and Ascot Hills Park.  

​The Los Angeles Unified School District (LAUSD) and The Los Angeles Fire Department (LAFD) have partnered in bringing the very first LAFD fire academy magnet school program to Woodrow Wilson High School in El Sereno, CA, joining the existing LAPD student police cadet program.

 
Join us on the best 3.1 mile trail course in East Los Angeles! 

Our 5K course will challenge all levels of runners, walkers and hikers.  The race is chip-timed for those seeking friendly competition and/or a chance to win a commemorative LAFD challenge coin.

​If you enjoy trail running, walking or hiking, you'll be certain to enjoy this event with spectacular views of Los Angeles, Dodger Stadium and the Hollywood sign, all visible from within the park.

name: Aut2Run for Autism (15K, 5K, 10K, Fun-K, 1 Mile & Virtual Race)
description:
We are excited to welcome you back to an in-person Aut2Run at California State University Channel Islands on Sunday, April 26th, 2026! For those of you who can't experience Aut2Run in-person, but would still like to support Autism Society Ventura County, we will be offering a virtual option for you to participate in. This year is extra special to us as we celebrate Aut2Run's 14th anniversary!

100% of the proceeds from Aut2Run go directly towards fulfilling Autism Society Ventura County's (ASVC) mission to create connections, empowering all with Autism to live fully. ASVC works to promote lifelong access and opportunity for all individuals within the autism spectrum and their families to be fully included members of the community. They achieve this through education, advocacy, a variety of programs, increasing public awareness, and collaboration with other agencies.

ASVC programs are primarily for individuals, families and caregivers who have people in their lives with autism of all ages. We also collaborate with service providers, agency staff, educators and teachers, and professionals who are interested in furthering the mission of ASVC. Their programs are open to any individual, family, or community member impacted by autism. Our Board consists of all dedicated volunteers.

In-Person Race Information: 

10K (1/2 Road & 1/2 Trail) Run - 7:00am Please note, we have a strict course time limit for the 10K. All participants must be able to complete the 10K in 75 minutes (that is a 12 minute per mile pace).  If you do not reach the University Park Entrance (heading back to the South Quad after the trail loop) in 54 minutes, you will be transported to where the 5K joins in at Channel Islands Dr and will receive a DNF (Did Not Finish).
5K Run/Walk - 8:45am
1 Mile Run/Walk - 10:15am
Fun-K - 10:45am This event is for children under age 12 and for adults with special needs and their caregivers. Limited to 300 participants.
15K Hero Run - Participants run both the 10K and 5K events separately. The times from the two races will be combined to give you your 15K results. 

Virtual Race Information & Instructions:
Please choose a local safe route (since this event is virtual you can run​ or walk anywhere you like, we recommend a place that is safe with limited interruptions).
Please follow all local laws, stop at all lights, stop signs and be careful when you cross at any cross walk. ​Please be aware of your surroundings and be cautious as you will not be running or walking on a closed course. We cannot emphasize this enough. 
Maintain, at an absolute minimum, 6ft between you and anyone else not in your household.

Your race packet will be mailed to you the week of the race. 

Tracking your Virtual Race Distance:

Please use a GPS watch or phone with a GPS app (Strava or RunKeeper or two good ones) to track your time and distance. Upon completion you will then add your distance and time onto https://www.aut2run.org/Race/Results/2323#resultSetId-289928;perpage:100 anytime between April 18th and May 1st. Please note, submissions are based on the honor system and there are not awards for the virtual run. 

Packet Pick Up Information:

We highly recommend that all race participants pick up their packets on Saturday!!

Saturday Packet Pickup will help you avoid VERY long lines and reduce anxiety on race morning. The race packet consists of your required race bib, t-shirt, and goodie bag. 

  • Saturday, April 25th 10:00am - 2:00pm at California State University Channel Islands (South Quad)
  • Sunday, April 26th 6:00am - 10:45am at  California State University Channel Islands (South Quad)
    • Please arrive at least 30 minutes prior to your event start time. Expect lines at race morning packet pick up.

For more info on the Aut2Run event go to http://www.aut2run.org/          
For more info on ASVC go to http://www.autismventura.org/

To visit our Donation Gift Store please click here https://squareup.com/store/autism-society-ventura-county

Please consider making a donation and raising funds to benefit Autism support in Ventura County!

ALL registered finishers will receive one of our unique finisher medals and a soft event t-shirt.  Additional t-shirts, hats and other items are available for purchase in limited quantities at the event.

Make sure to use #Aut2Run!

name: Autism on the Run
description:
We are excited to announce Autism on the Run. On April 11th, 2026 at the Park at Riverwalk in Bakersfield, California.  We will have a 10k, 5k, 2k, and family walk.

 

Pricing is $45 a person for 10k, 5k, 2k and includes a shirt and medal

Pricing for Family is $160 and includes 5 medals and 1 swag bag, (no shirts are included with this discount) 

 

April is Autism Awareness Month. Autism refers to a broad range of conditions characterized by challenges with social skills, repetitive behaviors, speech, and nonverbal communication.

 

This event benefits H.E.A.R.T.S. Connection Family Empowerment Center whose mission is to enhance the quality of life for people with special needs through a family-directed resource center that symbolizes professionalism, dignity, compassion, and respect.   For more information contact us at 661-328-9055.  This event will feature vendors, family fun, and raffles.

name: Avalon Benefit 50 Mile/50K Run
description: The Avalon Benefit 50 Mile/50K Run is the oldest Ultra Trail Run in California with the 50 Mile run entering its 43rd year.   The 50K joined the party six years ago and instantly became a California classic in trail running traversing all of the same trails that the older run uses.   Running the Avalon Benefit 50Mile/50K provides you a first rate, up-close and personal experience of one of California's natural jewels in trail running across Catalina Island.   The run begins and ends in Avalon and in between you simply have to run the entire length of the island - and back!  In between you will experience beautiful vistas, tremendous views of the Pacific Ocean, see a bison or two and experience some of the sports great volunteers and aid stations.

name: Aztlan XC Classic
description:
Aztlan XC Classic was established in 1976. It has been long due and now we welcome you back. This time, those who have competed at this event are now well into their 50s. You are now coaches, mentors, teachers, parents and even grandparents. Bring your family, team or if you're still challenging yourself then sign up and let’s celebrate our success.

This event exclusively benefits Aztlan Athletics Foundation (AAF). For details about the subsidized running camps, scholarships, and complimentary registrations visit AztlanAthleticsFoundation.org.

name: Back to the Future: 88 MPH Dash 5K, 10K & Half
description:
Back to the Future: 88 MPH Dash 5K, 10K & Half

October 17, 2026 · 7:00 a.m. PST · 6846 Owensmouth Ave, Canoga Park, CA

Get ready to rev up your DeLorean and hit 88 MPH! This race celebrates the iconic Back to the Future trilogy, with a special nod to Back to the Future Day—October 21—the 2015 date Marty McFly and Doc Brown traveled to the future in Back to the Future Part II.

Presented by Jed & Ted’s Excellent Races

Whether you're a time-traveling teen or a mad scientist, this race lets you channel your inner McFly and dash through time with style.

Choose your challenge:

  • 88 MPH Sprint 5K⚡ Perfect for those looking to make a quick getaway from 1985.
  • Twin Pines 10K 🌲 A tribute to the mall where it all began—before the pine trees were history.
  • Enchantment Under the Run Half Marathon 🎶 Dance through time and space in this nostalgic long-distance challenge.
  • The Multiverse Flux Capacitor Challenge (Virtual) 🌀 Can't make it in person? Join us virtually and complete any distance to earn your medal.

Expect time-traveling tunes, futuristic photo ops, and plenty of 80s nostalgia. Costumes encouraged—think puffer vests, lab coats, and hoverboards!



Parody Disclaimer
This race is a fan-made parody event inspired by 80s pop culture and is not affiliated with or endorsed by any official trademark holders.

name: Badwater 267 VR
description:
BADWATER: It’s a frame of mind, a global family of horizon-chasers, and a statement to the world about priorities and preconceived notions of what is possible. Badwater is a way of life! Are you ready to kick off the New Year with an authentic, original Badwater experience?

AdventureCORPS® – the organizers of the iconic worldwide series of Badwater® races – are pleased to offer the BADWATER 267 VR in which competitors virtually and sequentially traverse the routes of all three Badwater® races – the 51-mile Badwater Cape Fear, the 81-mile Badwater Salton Sea, and the 135-mile Badwater 135 – for a total of 267 miles, or 430km. These three events comprise the legendary Badwater Ultra Cup - and Badwater 267 VR! Start off the New Year with this new challenge and immerse yourself in the world of Badwater!

If you are up to the challenge, you will complete 267 miles (430km) during the month of January. You have 31 days to complete 267 miles on foot - or 133.5 miles swimming, 801 miles cycling  - and you can do them anywhere you want, including indoors. There is also a multi-sport division for those who want to combine different sports (including paddle sports, cross-country and downhill skiing, skateboarding, and more; see below.) Participation is based on the “honor system,” but there is a highly recommended - and very popular - Private Strava Club to bring everyone together.

Go at your own pace, as often or as long as you want, wherever you live, anywhere on the planet! 

Guidelines:

• Running Division: You must complete all 267 miles on foot: This includes Walking, Hiking, Snowshoeing, and Treadmill, whether indoors or outdoors, covering 267 miles (430km) in 31 days. This is the Running Division, in which ONLY these bipedal activities may be counted. Also Note: In the Strava app, always log any of these activities as "Running" so that they appear on the club leaderboard.

NOTE: Elliptical is NOT allowed in the Running Division. 

• Multi-Sport division: MANY sports may be included, besides, cycling, swimming, and running: All paddle and rowing sports, ice-skating, rollerblading, skateboarding, and cross-country skiing are also allowed in the multi-sport category, and all they all count one-for-one.

name: Badwater Presents 40/40 NOW: Creating Balance in an Ultra World
description:
40/40 NOW, presented by AdventureCORPS: May 13 - June 21, 2026

 

Creating Balance in an Ultra World

 

We invite you to join us for a very special, first of its kind, 40-Day Life Adventure!

 

40/40 NOW is a 40-day program which can serve many purposes:

-              Cross-Training for Sport, and for Life

-              Celebrate the Summer Solstice as your Best Self

-              For Ultra Athletes: Sharpen your Body and Mind for the Summer Racing Season

 

40 / 40 NOW is open to anyone and everyone! (While we are the people behind the world-wide series of BADWATER® Ultramarathons, this opportunity is for anybody looking to head into summer as their very best self.)

 

Duration: 40 Days, from Wednesday, May 13 through Sunday, June 21.  

(The 2026 summer solstice is on Sunday, June 21, 2026 at 1:24 AM.)

 

Why 40 Days? 30 Days Creates a Habit, but a 40 Day Effort is a Spiritual Odyssey.

 

What Is the 40/40 Path? How does it work? What's involved? 

 

The core of this challenge is completing 40 minutes of intentional movement activities in the AM, and 40 minutes in the PM.        

-              One must be strength and/or flexibility oriented. Think weightlifting, yoga, stretch class, dance class, or martial arts. (This can be done at a gym or fitness studio, but also on your own at home, following DVDs or YouTube classes.)

 

-              The other 40-minute activity will be cardio-oriented. Think running, walking, hiking, bicycling, skating, or swimming. (For participants who already run or bike well over 40 minutes per day, we recommend pursuing a different sport for this 40-minute cardio activity.)

 

Additionally, each participant will check-In daily in the Strava Club: Given that participants will be all over the world, each morning (Pacific Time) we will post a “Daily Check-In!” reminder in the Strava Club: Every participant will comment to tell us what they did – and perhaps learned – that day after their PM activity. Accountability makes it real! Teamwork makes the dream work!

 

40/40 participants will also pursue ten different four-day personal challenges, and take “brain breaks” every Sunday: 

-              10 Personal Challenges: One will be announced every Four Days

-              Screen-Free Sundays: No digital noise for 8 hours: You pick the timeframe, as long as it's during waking hours. (If work or childcare means you need your phone close, keep the ringer on for notifications, or have a family member or friend be in charge of your phone. Or if you must be on your phone, just don’t scroll any social media.)

-              Also every Sunday: Pause and Celebrate!  This is the opposite of a To Do List, this is a Done List: Write it and celebrate all you’ve achieved today, or in the past four days, or in the past week!

Every day each participant will receive an email which contains:

-              An inspiring quote

-              A simple but powerful nutrition tip and/or recipe

-              A link to an inspiring online or social media talk

-              Also, every four days, the email will announce the next of the ten 4-Day Challenges

 

The 40/40 participants will receive a printed interactive guidebook containing: 

-              “The Power and Meaning of 40”

-              “The Power and Meaning of the Summer Solstice”

-              Recommended Reading List: 40 Books that could Change Your Life

-              Hints at the ten Four-Day Challenges (actual Challenge details will come by email, so there’s no “planning ahead” – part of the challenge is the surprise!)

-              40-Day Calendar to track your progress: May 13-June 21, 2026

 

 

HOW WILL 40/40 NOW PARTICIPANTS INTERACT?

                  For camaraderie and to share insights and inspirations, a special, private Strava Club will bring everyone together on an ongoing, daily basis.

 

WHAT HAPPENS ON DAY 1?

• You will study the 40 / 40 NOW Guidebook

• You will write a note to yourself about what you hope to gain from this, how you feel your life is now (where are you happy or unhappy, how you want to become a better version of yourself.) You will put this is an envelope and set it aside for 40 days.

• You will begin! – Your AM and PM 40-minute activities, and the first of the four-day personal challenges.

 

WHAT HAPPENS ON DAY 40? THE END IS JUST THE BEGINNING > COMING TOGETHER ON THE SUMMER SOLSTICE

 

With the arrival of the Summer Solstice, we will celebrate and “seal” this experience in several ways:

 

• First, you will read your Day 1 Challenged note to yourself. Whether you share about this in the Strava Club is entirely up to you; no pressure to “over share”!

• We will send out a few simple Rituals to Celebrate the Summer Solstice; choose one or more!

• You will post your final AM and PM activities to the Strava Club and log them in your printed 40 / 40 NOW Guidebook.

• Zoom Call: We will all come together for a 40-minute video chat via  Zoom; this will take place at 900am, Pacific Time. (There will be participants all over the world, but this time works best for those in the Western Hemisphere and Europe.)

 

FINALLY, some  Mementos will be sent to each participant after  40/40 NOW concludes:

40/40 NOW Keychain (Very high quality, meant to last!)

40/40 NOW T-shirt

40/40 NOW Decal

Delivered in a Custom 40/40 NOW Box

name: Badwater Salton Sea, presented by Mount to Coast
description:
The BADWATER® ultra running experience returns to the Anza-Borrego Desert and Palomar Mountain when the twelfth BADWATER SALTON SEA - presented by Mount to Coast - race takes place on April 26-27, 2025.

 

This remarkable event challenges teams of two or three ultrarunners – running together as duos or trios for the duration, NOT in a relay – to tackle an unimaginable traverse of Southern California deserts and mountains. The  route covers 81 miles (130km) from Salton City (elevation 234 feet / 71m below sea level) to Palomar Mountain, the almost tallest mountain in San Diego County (elevation 5500 feet / 1676m.)* Eight of the 81 race miles pass through Anza-Borrego State Park on a single track trail from Borrego Springs to Ranchita, creating a race route which is a mix of road and trail. There is a total elevation gain of over 9000 feet (2740m).

The eleven previous editions were received with wide acclaim. The thirteenth edition – with a limit of 100 runners – is scheduled for April 18-19 (Saturday-Sunday), 2026.

RACE DIFFICULTY

This is an extremely difficult race held in extreme conditions: Veterans of this event routinely state that it is as hard as any of the toughest 100 milers they have done.

The extreme weather changes - from 100+F / 38+C during the day, often with a sand storm, to freezing temperates with very wet fog at night - along with the extreme challenge of the two major mountain ascents - combine to make this an extremely difficult race.

It is critical to train properly for the heat and to train effectively for very steep desert single-track trail section of the race which is done in maximum heat and without the support crew nearby. Additionally, the single track trail is VERY steep and surprises runners every year with both its steepness, rugged terrain, and intense heat. Knowledge of maintaining proper electrolyte balance is also critical. Study the relevant articles at Badwater University closely, as well as race reports from former competitors.

Team Format

Unique to Badwater® Salton Sea is a “Team Ultra Racing” format: All race entrants must enter and race as teams of two or three runners (all male, all female, or co-ed divisions), remaining together for the duration – NOT in a relay format – and sharing just one support vehicle with at least two crew members.

 

We encourage each runner to select teammates with compatible running style and pace, and with whom he or she would really like to share this experience!

 

Divisions are offered for All Male, All Female, and Mixed (for 3x teams, 2 men and 1 woman, or 1 man and 2 women, are considered equal).

 

Some teams have come together in the past through the wonders of the internet, for example through our Facebook Event Page for each year’s event, or just through personal social media (and real world!) connections!

 

It is very important to pick good teammates to have an ideal experience at this race, and to have the highest likelihood of the whole team finishing together, intact, which SHOULD BE the goal of every team in the race. Here’s what we suggest:

 

– Invite runners that you have run with a lot, and find you have compatible speeds, styles (pacing, how much time you spend getting aid, etc.), and temperament (sense of humour, how much you like to talk versus staying quiet or listening to music, etc.). Those could be runners in your club or with whom you train a lot. But that could also be runners who don’t live near you, but you only see at races.

 

– Think about all the races you do. Aren’t there others who consistently finish right near you in lots of races? Seems like a good place to start with picking a teammate, don’t you think?

 

– Taking that a step further, why not pick teammates with whom you actually compete directly? Again, you’re likely about the same speed, so why not work together instead of against each other, for a change? Why not “bury the hatchet,” so to speak?

 

– What about fellow runners that you are mentoring, whether “formally” or just in a friendly way? Why not help another runner have an amazing experience in your company, with you playing the role of “grizzled old veteran” or Jedi of ultra running? There is no Luke Skywalker without Obi-Wan Kenobi, after all.

 

Anyway, those are a few ideas for not only picking good teammates, but also for having an exemplary experience, something that will really be transcendent, and meaningful, and will resonate far and beyond after the race is over and you’ve – hopefully – gone home with your buckles.

 

QUALIFYING REQUIREMENTS: Entry may be denied to those without sufficient endurance credentials. All applicants must have completed at least one difficult 50-mile ultramarathon in the previous 12 months prior to entry. Proof of this qualification must be included within the entry application OR by email at least 60 days prior to the race. Completing one or more tough 100-milers before this event is highly recommended, as is experience in desert heat racing. Veterans of this event routinely state that it is as hard or harder than any of the toughest 100 milers they have done.

 

REFUND POLICY: Generally speaking, it is our expectation that registered teams will not withdraw from this event. Instead, if one runner has to withdraw from the race, he or she will be replaced with a new teammate, at the discretion of the remaining runner(s) on the team. There are no transfers of registration, nor roll-overs to the next year. Entry fee refunds, less 25%, will be offered until 60 days prior to the event. After that, there are no refunds, nor roll-overs or credits.

 

ALL TEAMMATES MUST ENTER ON THE SAME WEEK: Please submit all teammates’ registrations and payments on the same day or within a few days. No runner or team is considered fully registered until ALL runners on the team are registered and paid in full. Runners who register, but don’t have a full team registered within two weeks, may be dropped from the roster and issued a refund, less 25%.

 

EVENT CANCELLATION: If the event is canceled due to pandemic, hurricane, community disaster, or other force majeure, neither refunds nor credits will be given.

 

ROUTE APPROVALS: Although we anticipate using the same or nearly the same route each year, the final, exact route is subject to approval from various government agencies and is always subject to change due to various factors beyond our control.

 

Visit our Badwater.com website for more information!

name: Bayside Saved by the Bell 5K, 10K & Half Marathon
description:
September 19, 2026 · 7:00 a.m. PST · 6846 Owensmouth Ave, Canoga Park, CA

Get ready to dash through time in The Bayside Dash, a 90s high school sitcom-themed race packed with retro vibes, school spirit, and Slater-strength energy.

Presented by Jed & Ted’s Excellent Races

Whether you’re more Morris or Turtle, this race lets you channel your inner Bayside Tiger and crush your course with a smile.

  • Friends Forever 5K 🎶 Named after Zack Attack’s legendary ballad—because you don’t leave your squad behind on race day.
  • Time Out 10K✋ Inspired by Morris himself—freeze time, catch your breath, and own the course.
  • Hall Pass Half Marathon🎓 Go the distance like you’ve got a free pass to run the school (and the streets of Canoga Park).
  • The Multiverse Transfer Student Challenge (Virtual) 🌀 “Transfer Students” from any timeline can choose any distance and still earn their medal.

Expect high school pep rally energy, ‘Saved by the Bell’ moments, throwback tunes, and surprise “pop quizzes” of encouragement along the course. Costumes encouraged—go full Bayside or show off your best 90s teen energy.

This is a Jed & Ted’s Excellent Race—fun, fast, and full of nostalgia.

Sign up now. No hall pass required.

 

 

**Parody Disclaimer**  
This race is a fan-made parody event inspired by 90s pop culture and is not affiliated with or endorsed by any official trademark holders.

name: BE YOU 5K/10K
description:
Be You: The World Will Adjust

Lace up exactly as you are - because this run isn’t about fitting in, keeping pace, or chasing someone else’s finish line. The Be You 5K/10K encourages you to show up authentically, move proudly, and run (or walk, jog, strut, vibe) in your own lane! Whether you’re fast, slow, loud, quiet, glittery, introverted, extra, or just here for the shirt—THIS RACE CELEBRATES YOU!

Sign up for the BE YOU 5K/10K, complete it anytime and anywhere, and help give back to a great cause! Every entry gets you a custom high-quality shirt that is sure to be your new favorite, a cool finisher medal, along with a donation to Stand Up To Cancer in order to help SU2C get one step closer to its mission of making everyone diagnosed with cancer a survivor! No Pace. No Pressure. Just BE YOU.

TO JOIN: 

  • Register for the BE YOU 5K/10K before March 31st, 2026
  • Complete a 5K (3.1 miles) or 10K (6.2 miles) at your convenience any time anywhere (no deadline)!
  • Celebrate your accomplishment by sharing on social media! #BeYou5K10K #IRun4Movement

name: Because of Sadie 5K
description: We lost our amazing, beautiful daughter on January 31, 2022. She was just 14 years old. After contracting COVID, we received the devastating news that she also was diagnosed with leukemia. The combination of both diagnoses was too much for her body to handle and we lost her just 33 days later. Help us turn grief into joy. We volunteered often through the National Charity League. Walk, jog, or run in Sadie's honor to support her favorite philanthropy, Retrievers and Friends of Southern CA. They are an all-volunteer, non-profit organization devoted to finding homes for dogs and cats. Sadie enjoyed spending time there socializing animals, doing laundry, and cleaning the kennels. A portion of every registration fee will be donated to them.

name: Bedrock Valley Gravel Ride
description:
BEDROCK VALLEY GRAVEL RIDE

A Gravel Ride experience you don't want to miss. Choose your ride experience around Diamond Valley Lake. This is truly a historic ride in an ancient place. This area's heritage begins during the Ice Age where the most concentrated amount of Mastodons once roam the earth. The remains of hundreds of Mastodons and other prehistoric dinosaurs were discovered in the bedrock of where the lake now rests.

NEW! GRAVEL ROCK BIKE RACE is the first Gravel Bike race that takes you around the Lake. Ride Gravel/Mountain/E-Bike

GRAVEL ROCK RIDE 36K takes you ONE LOOP around beautiful Diamond Valley Lake. Great for your first Gravel/Off-Road Ride

GRAVEL ROCK RIDE 72K takes you TWO LOOPS around beautiful Diamond Valley Lake. Test your skills and make it a double.

GRAVEL ROCK RIDE 108K takes you THREE LOOPS around beautiful Diamond Valley Lake. Find your limits and test your endurance.

GRAVEL KIDS 10K is a fun and flat fun ride for the spirited rider/beginner. An out and back course that gets you stoked!

TEAM CHALLENGE enjoy the ride with friends and complete laps as a team in the 72k and 108k.

name: Bedrock Valley Trail Runs
description:
BEDROCK VALLEY TRAIL RUNS

The Bedrock Valley Trail Runs is a NEW trail running experience you don't want to miss. We offer something for the whole family to enjoy. Choose from the beautiful  Bedrock Valley Trail Marathon, Trail Half Marathon, 15k, 5k, Stroller 5k and bring the kids for the the 1 Mile Kid's Fun Run around Diamond Valley Lake. This is truly a historic run in an ancient place. This area's heritage begins during the Ice Age where the most concentrated amount of Mastodons once roam the earth. The remains of hundreds of Mastodons and other prehistoric dinosaurs were discovered in the bedrock of where the lake now rests.

TRAIL MARATHON is a great introduction into trail marathons. A relatively flat loop around the lake ending with some beautiful single track with small climbs. Ideal for all running levels.

TRAIL HALF MARATHON is a beautiful out and back section along the lake bed and perfect for accomplishing your first half marathon.

15K course challenges the runner with a little of everything: flat, fast, climbing, descending on the famous Wildflower single track trail.

NEW! 10K is a fast out and back with views of the lake.

NEW! STAMPEDE 5K is a fast and flat out and back. Great for a fast run or hike. 

SOARING 5K is a great distance through the stunning Wildflower Trails. Great for a quick run or hike. This course does take you up and down the trails finishing along the shoreline.

STROLLER TRAIL 5k our first specific stroller only 5k is a beautiful flat 3.1 miles out and back. Enjoy with the little ones.

KID'S 1 MILE FUN RUN is open to children 10 and younger. This is a non-timed run. All kids receive a finisher’s medal and other goodies.

NEW! GRAVEL ROCK BIKE RACE is the first Gravel Bike race that takes you around the Lake. Ride Gravel/Mountain/E-Bike

We are a CUPLESS race series. Please make sure to bring some form of hydration vessel to carry hydration for your event. There will not be cups provided at aid stations.

Choose from the beautiful  Bedrock Valley Trail Marathon, Trail Half Marathon, 15k, 5k, Stroller 5k and bring the kids for the the 1 Mile Kid's Fun Run around Diamond Valley Lake. This is truly a historic run in an ancient place. This area's heritage begins during the Ice Age where the most concentrated amount of Mastodons once roam the earth. The remains of hundreds of Mastodons and other prehistoric dinosaurs were discovered in the bedrock of where the lake now rests.

TRAIL MARATHON is a great introduction into trail marathons. A relatively flat loop around the lake ending with some beautiful single track with small climbs. Ideal for all running levels.

TRAIL HALF MARATHON is a beautiful out and back section along the lake bed and perfect for accomplishing your first half marathon.

15K course challenges the runner with a little of everything: flat, fast, climbing, descending on the famous Wildflower single track trail.

NEW! 10K is a fast out and back with views of the lake.

NEW! STAMPEDE 5K is a fast and flat out and back. Great for a fast run or hike. 

SOARING 5K is a great distance through the stunning Wildflower Trails. Great for a quick run or hike. This course does take you up and down the trails finishing along the shoreline.

STROLLER TRAIL 5k our first specific stroller only 5k is a beautiful flat 3.1 miles out and back. Enjoy with the little ones.

KID'S 1 MILE FUN RUN is open to children 10 and younger. This is a non-timed run. All kids receive a finisher’s medal and other goodies.

NEW! GRAVEL ROCK BIKE RACE is the first Gravel Bike race that takes you around the Lake. Ride Gravel/Mountain/E-Bike

We are a CUPLESS race series. Please make sure to bring some form of hydration vessel to carry hydration for your event. There will not be cups provided at aid stations.

name: Bee Sweet Citrus Farm-K
description:
Join the Bee Sweet Citrus and Ag One teams on Saturday, February 7, 2026, for our inaugural Farm-K event! This run/walk is a family-friendly event that benefits the next generation of agriculturalists, and we'd love for you to join in on the fun. 

Register for our timed 5k or our 1 Mile Walk in support of the Fresno State Ag One Foundation!

The event takes place at Fresno State's O'Niell Park, and all participants earn an event shirt and a custom finisher's medallion.

name: Beginning "Learn-By-Doing" Pole Vault Clinic For Coaches & Athletes
description:
A hands-on introduction to safe, effective pole-vault coaching and beginner athlete development.

Clinic Plan:

Participants will rotate through stations led by 4–6 accomplished coaches, covering:

How to hold and carry the pole

Plant mechanics

Running technique and take-off

Introduction to sand vaulting

Possible progression to pit vaulting based on safety and athlete readiness

name: Bell Gardens 5K
description: Bell Gardens 5K course is designed to provide fast times, and it’s ideal for spectators. This is a two-loop course that covers flat wide public streets of Bell Gardens. Participants will start at Veterans park at the corner of Perry and Suva, head east towards Scout Street, then back to complete the loop on Florence Place. Making a turn on Perry then onto lap 2. A water station will be available at the start of the second loop. The Kid's 1/2 mile is out and back on Suva Street. The road will be completely closed to traffic.

name: Besties Run 5K. 10K. Half Marathon
description:
📅 Sunday, February 8, 2026
📍 5400 E Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA 90803

  
✨Grab your bestie— and get ready to celebrate the women who lift you up and run beside you through life’s ups and downs. Or come out solo and make new friends who cheer you on every step of the way. 
This isn’t just a run — it’s a movement for connection, confidence, and community. ✨

 

✨WHAT’S INCLUDED WITH REGISTRATION:

CERTIFIED COURSE

CHIP TIMING

FINISHER MEDAL

RACE BIB

RACE PHOTOS

RACE T-SHIRT

LIVE DJ & FINISH LINE PARTY

VENDORS & GIVEAWAYS

FOOD & REFRESHMENTS

SCENIC COASTAL COURSE ALONG THE LONG BEACH, BEACH PATH

 

✨About the Besties Option- Running is better together!

Our Besties Run entries are specially designed for duos — two registrations bundled together at a special reduced rate, so you and your bestie can cross the finish line side by side and save money.
Make this your Galentine’s tradition!

PLEASE NOTE : ONCE YOU PURCHASE "BESTIE" OPTION SECOND RUNNER WILL BE ADDED VIA EMAIL THAT WILL BE SENT OUT BEFORE BIB PICK UP DAY.

✨Why We Run Together
This event is all about women supporting women — cheering each other on, and proving we can do hard things together. 

 

✨All Paces, All Abilities, All Welcome
Runners and walkers are welcome.Whether you’re chasing a PR or enjoying a stroll with your squad, you’re part of the movement. 


✨Run Club Girls is proud to bring this empowering event to life — a celebration of sisterhood, self-love, and shared strength.

 

Event Management by CaliFlow Runs — where heart, hustle, and high vibes power every mile.

name: Beyond The Streets 5k, 10k & Half Marathon
description:
Jed & Ted's Excellent Races proudly present the second annual Beyond The Streets 5K, 10K & Half Marathon.

Join us on February 7, 2026 at 7:00 a.m. as we take over the headwaters of the Los Angeles River near Canoga Park High School. This run is all about the real LA River experience, the sights, the sounds, the quiet moments, the unexpected pockets of life. and the community that moves along it.

This event is FREE, but we encourage donations. Every dollar goes directly to North Valley Caring Services, supporting the people and families who need it most. You’ll see an option to donate during registration.

We're making this event free because we want everyone to be able to show up, move their body, and be part of something good: no barriers, no pressure, no financial gatekeeping. But if you’re able to donate, even a little, it makes a real difference.

All donations go directly to North Valley Caring Services, an organization doing hands-on work with people experiencing homelessness, food insecurity, and crisis right here in the Valley. They run meal programs, hygiene services, family support programs, and help folks get back on their feet with dignity and real, practical assistance.

Think of it this way:

WE cover the race. YOU cover what you can. TOGETHER we lift up our neighbors.

If this run brings you joy, clarity, community, or a sense of purpose, consider sharing some of that forward. Every dollar goes straight to NVCS, and every dollar helps someone move beyond survival and toward stability.

Come be part of something meaningful and memorable, the start of a race that grows with the river, the city, and the community around it.

Race day packet pick up will be available Saturday March 7th from 6:45am - 7:45am
Any questions about registration or packet pick up please email shawna@fleetfeetchico.com
 

 

START DATE & TIMES
When: Saturday March 7th, 2026

5K, 10k and Half Marathon run and fun walk: Starting time is 8:00am for the 5k and 8:10 for the 10k and Half Marathon.
 
Entry fees are non-refundable and non-transferable.
For special school group rates contact shawna@fleetfeetchico.com
 
Every registered runner will receive a 2026 race shirt if registered before February 6th. To guarantee your shirt size please register on or before February 6th. All registrations after February 6th will be subject to availability and size at packet pickup. Any leftover shirts after packet pick up will be available after the race at the Fleet Feet booth starting at 9:00am. 
If still running, you may have someone pick up a shirt for you. Please provide them your name and or bib #.
If you do not pick up your packet before the race (at packet pickup or at the race), your shirt will NOT be saved for you. 
 
COURSE CERTIFICATION AND MAPS
 
The 5k and 10k are flat, paved, and free of traffic. The half marathon has a 1/4 mile on each of the loops that are a single-track trail. All events start and finish at One Mile Recreation Area in Lower Bidwell Park.
 
The maps to all the racecourses can be found by clicking the link below:
Race Maps - Fleet Feet Chico
 

 

Shake out run Event!

Join us on March 6th at 6:00pm at Fleet Feet Chico for an easy evening shakeout run. We will go for a short run 3-6 mile run/walk and enjoy a cold beverage and come delicious carbs before the race. More information to come as we get closer to the event!

Location: Fleet Feet Chico, 241 Main St., Chico CA

Time: Show up between 5:30-6:00pm. Groups will start running at 6:15pm

 
PACKET PICKUP
 
Packet pickup will be offered at Fleet Feet Chico (241 Main St in downtown Chico) We will also have a small window on race day to pick up your packet.
 
Packet Pickup days and hours: 
 
Friday March 6th at Fleet Feet Chico
10:00am - 4:00pm
 
Located at Fleet Feet Chico, 241 Main St., Chico CA
 
Race Day Packet Pick up at the Fleet Feet Tent
6:45am-7:45am ONLY

 

RACE SHIRTS:


Race shirts are a unisex cotton shirt printed by Arroyo (formally Upper Park Printing) To be guaranteed a shirt in your size, you need to register on or before February 6th, 2026. All registration entries received after 2/6/26 will have shirts based on limited availability on a first come first serve basis.

 
DIRECTIONS AND PARKING
 
To the course: Enter Chico via Highway 99 either from the north or from the south. If you are coming from the north on 99, take the Highway 32 offramp and turn right at the first intersection. If you are coming from the south on 99, take the 32 offramp and turn left at the second intersection. Now you're heading west on 32 (East 8th St). From here, take 8th St just under a half-mile, then turn right on Sycamore St.

Sycamore St runs a few blocks into Woodland Ave, which runs parallel to the park. The park itself will be closed to vehicle traffic on race day, so find a parking spot on or near Woodland Ave. Please be courteous and park legally. Do not park in a way that blocks local residents' entry to or exit from their homes. There are several entrances to the One Mile Recreation Area from Woodland Ave. 

To Fleet Feet packet pickup: As above, from Highway 99 head west on Highway 32 (East 8th St).
Take 8th St about a mile then turn right on Main St. Drive north on Main St. Fleet Feet is located between 2nd and 3rd Streets. Fleet Feet's phone number is 530 345-1000.
 
TIMING
Timing will be done by Bizz Johnson Racing. All races will be a gun start and a chip finish. If you are racing for an overall placement, you must toe the line! (Based on Gun time/first to cross the line)
 
Gun start for 5k will be at 8:00am
Gun start for 10k, and Half Marathon will be 8:10am
 

AID STATIONS AND RESTROOMS
There will be 6 aid stations for the half, 3 for the 10k and 2 for the 5k.
1.     Cedar Grove Bathrooms – Loop 1 Water / Loop 2 Water, nutrition gels and electrolytes 
2.     Peterson Drive Gate – Loop 1 Water / Loop 2 Water, nutrition gels and electrolytes 
3.     One Mile Parking Lot on Vallombrosa Side – Water and electrolytes 
Restroom on the course will be located at One Mile recreation on the North and South side of the pool, Cedar Grove Park, and Pettersen Dr. Park entrance as well as portable restrooms at the start and finish.
 
RULES
 
  • Please no dogs on the course during the race. Stollers are allowed, please be cautious of other runners. If wearing headphones, only in one ear please! Must be able to hear your surroundings.
  • Be courteous when overtaking slower runners or walkers in your elected race location. We want you to race hard and fast, but with safety of yourself and others in mind. (Please remember that this is a public park and there may be others on course that are not part of the race)
     
  • Where your Race number so it is visible on the participant's front
  • Run your race with pride!
  • You must cross the timing mat for your chip to be read. If you are planning of racing for top finisher, the race is based on gun time and first to cross the finish line.
  • Run, hard, run fast and have fun!
     
 
AWARDS FOR TOP FINISHERS
 
We will be offering a CASH PRIZE Top male and female for each race! (5k, 10k and Half) We will have an award ceremony at 8:45am for the 5k, 9:15am for the 10k and 10:00am for the Half Marathon races.
 
Age group awards can be found at the Fleet Feet tent following the award ceremony for each race. 
(Awards will also be offered to the top three in each age group category for each gender in each race)
 
All unclaimed prized will be available for pick up at Fleet Feet Chico on Sunday March 8th during regular business hours. (11:00am-4:00pm)
 
Ages groups will be as followed: 
14 and under / 15-19 / 20-29 / 30-39 / 40-49 / 50-59 / 60-69 / 70 and over
 
Finisher Medals will be provided to all Half Marathon runners who finish the race.
(Any remaining medals will be available for pick up at Fleet Feet Chico for 5k and 10k runners on Sunday March 8th)
 
 
Please visit www.fleetfeetchico.com for more information or email shawna@fleetfeetchico.com

name: Big River Adventure
description:
Welcome to the 25th annual Big River Adventure!

Join us for a unique race experience where you can choose your adventure to run, swim, walk, or paddle your way through the scenic beauty of Mendocino County's Big River.

For the past 25 years, Cancer Resource Centers of Mendocino County has been bringing our community together for this special fundraising event. While the activities may change from year to year, our mission remains steadfast: to honor and remember those impacted by cancer, and to raise vital funds to support free services for individuals facing cancer in Mendocino County.

Starting at the Big River boat launch, participants will embark on a journey filled with stunning views and the shared goal of making a difference in the lives of others.

Don't miss out on this unforgettable adventure! Register now and be part of something truly meaningful.

To keep this family-friendly event affordable and accessible to our community, we will not be providing t-shirts this year.

Here is a link to a trail map

•             5k runners will run east on the haul road to the 5k turn around.

•             10k runners dash east on the haul road to the 10K turn around (10K map).

•             5k "Fun" Walkers will follow the 5k runners route.

•             Kiddie run will begin at the boat launch

•             Swimmers will dive in at the boat lunch and swim east up Big River

•             Paddlers will begin at the boat launch and paddle east up Big River  *Please note you must bring your own vessel.

There are multiple race age divisions. Note: Participants between the ages of 6 and 17 may enter any race division at a discounted rate of $20 at signup.

Race Contact Info

Phone / Teléfono: (707) 937-3833

E-mail / Correo electrónico: info@crcmendocino.org

name: Big River Adventure
description:
Welcome to the 25th annual Big River Adventure!

Join us for a unique race experience where you can choose your adventure to run, swim, walk, or paddle your way through the scenic beauty of Mendocino County's Big River.

For the past 25 years, Cancer Resource Centers of Mendocino County has been bringing our community together for this special fundraising event. While the activities may change from year to year, our mission remains steadfast: to honor and remember those impacted by cancer, and to raise vital funds to support free services for individuals facing cancer in Mendocino County.

Starting at the Big River boat launch, participants will embark on a journey filled with stunning views and the shared goal of making a difference in the lives of others.

Don't miss out on this unforgettable adventure! Register now and be part of something truly meaningful.

To keep this family-friendly event affordable and accessible to our community, we will not be providing t-shirts this year.

Here is a link to a trail map

•             5k runners will run east on the haul road to the 5k turn around.

•             10k runners dash east on the haul road to the 10K turn around (10K map).

•             5k "Fun" Walkers will follow the 5k runners route.

•             Kiddie run will begin at the boat launch

•             Swimmers will dive in at the boat lunch and swim east up Big River

•             Paddlers will begin at the boat launch and paddle east up Big River  *Please note you must bring your own vessel.

There are multiple race age divisions. Note: Participants between the ages of 6 and 17 may enter any race division at a discounted rate of $20 at signup.

name: Bike The Coast
description:
Experience gorgeous riding along pristine beaches, historic Pacific Coast Highway, iconic beach landmarks and unique, Southern California weather with the annual Bike The Coast Bike Tour.   Select from distances of 25 mile, 50 mile, and 100 mile rides and then come out and ride along with 2000 other enthusiast along some of Southern California's best-known cities and roadways.  When you finish, meet us back at  the Oceanside pier to celebrate with your selection of food options, a lively beer garden, great music and new friends.

This is a truly bucket list event if you are an avid rider who enjoys getting some exercise, having fun, and experience great November weather.  This is a 'rules of the road' ride so come prepared to obey all traffic laws.

name: Bizz Johnson
description:
Set PRs and qualify for the Boston Marathon on this fast, downhill course! Total net downhill loss for the marathon is 929 feet making it the PERFECT course to qualify on! Per official B.A.A. confirmation, there will be no time penalties assessed for this course.

All races in 2026 will be Sunday, October 11. The marathon and 50K start at 8:00 AM at Mason Station Trailhead on McCoy Road with an out-and-back before jumping onto the Bizz Johnson Trail at Mason Station where the races travel through scenic Lassen National Forest. The first few miles of the course climb approximately 280 feet through the forest to Westwood Junction, then it’s downhill to the finish at Susanville, with a 1300-foot descent over the final 20 miles. The trail follows the route of the old Fernley and Lassen Branch Line of the Southern Pacific Railroad, built in 1914.

Roughly two-thirds of the way through the race, the trail enters the Susan River Canyon. Here, you’ll pass orange cliffs and cross the river ten times on picturesque wooden railroad bridges. About four miles from the finish, you’ll pass through two former railroad tunnels, 800 feet and 450 feet in length.

The Express Half Marathon starts at at 9:00 AM at Goumaz Campground which is Mile 14 of the full marathon route. After a short up-and-back, the Express Half Marathon flies down the Bizz Johnson to the finish.

Starting at Devil's Corral, the new Express 10K on Sunday does the last 6.2 miles of the full marathon. This course promises to be a fast, fun race. 

For all four events, you will be bused to a remote start.

PACKET PICKUP

  • Saturday Noon - 6 PM (50K, Marathon, Express Half Marathon, Express 10K): Susanville Historic Train Depot, 601 Richmond Road
  • Sunday Morning 6 AM - 7AM (Marathon and 50K), 7AM - 8 AM (Express Half Marathon and Express 10K): Susanville Historic Train Depot, 601 Richmond Road

PLEASE visit our website for maps, schedules, and all the important details!!

USAT&F certified full marathon course (CA18035RS)
