name: Davis Moonlight Run
description:
Event Day:

Saturday night, July 18, 2026

Four Events:

  • 5K, 10K, 10 Mile, 2K (approx. 1.25 miles)

Registration Opens:

March 2nd - Deal Days will run from March 2 to March 13, 2026

Event Details:

The Davis Moonlight Run will take place at Schilling Robotics, 201 Cousteau Place in Davis. The event begins at 7:50 pm with the 10 Mile and 10K, followed by the 5K and 2K at 8:00 pm. Courses are flat and travel along city streets as well as Davis' well-loved greenbelts. 10K, 10 Mile and 5K participants with an estimated finish greater than 45:00 are strongly encouraged to wear a headlamp or bring a flashlight for visibility along the course(s) in the dark. At the finish line, participants will be greeted with a heavyweight finisher medal (yes, it's cow-themed) and live music. Post-race activities include refreshments (including pizza by the slice, available for purchase), complimentary sno-cones, beer samples (21+) and awards distribution (for age group and our unique special divisions; see below for more details).  A dri-blend short sleeved race t-shirt is included with each entry; we also offer the ability to upgrade to a tank top (men's and women's sizing; 100% polyester fabric). Please note that dogs are not permitted in this race due to our race insurance, unless they are service animals. Wheelchairs and pushed wheelchairs for disabled athletes are permitted. 

Your entry to the Davis Moonlight Run includes the following*:

  • T-shirt included in entry (option to opt-out and save $5)
  • Finisher's medal
  • Age Group awards 
  • Special Division eligibility
  • Post-race music, suds, and snacks
  • Finish under the stars! 

*One complimentary beer to those 21+. Sno cones available for everyone including those who do not consume alcohol or who are designated driver. Additional beers available for donation. 

2026 Start Times


6:30 PM – Race Night Registration Opens
7:50 PM – 10 Mile and 10K Start
8:00 PM – 5K and 2K Start
10:00 PM – Cut Off For Course Support
10:15 PM – Finish Line Breakdown

Note: at this time of the year it gets dark at approximately 8:40 pm.
Start times are subject to change. Last updated 12/17/25.

Packet Pick Up

Bib and T-shirt pick up is held on race night starting at 6:30pm. Arrive an hour prior to your race start to have sufficient time to pick up, warm up, use restrooms, etc. Remember, hydrate all day so that you are well-hydrated for your run/walk.

Beneficiary: Cancer Champions

A Change of Pace is proud to announce our continued relationship with Cancer Champions as our ongoing charitable partner. Cancer Champions is a 501(c)(3) non-profit dedicated to supporting cancer survivors through custom fitness, nutrition, and mindset programming tailored to the unique needs of those battling or recovering from cancer treatment. Donations to Cancer Champions enable the organization to provide survivors with expert guidance to complement traditional cancer treatment. A Change of Pace and Cancer Champions both believe in the powerful and proven benefits of exercise, and we are very happy to be able to deepen our relationship in the name of health, fitness, and quality of life.

Location & Parking

All races start and finish at the same location, at Schilling Robotics, 201 Cousteau Place, Davis, CA 95618. Parking (free) is available in the adjacent business parks off Cousteau Place on the east side of Cousteau. 

Course Maps

Scroll to the bottom of this page to view course maps. Aid stations along the routes (denoted by a W on the map) will offer water and Gatorade. Please carry fluids with you if you are accustomed to drinking them more frequently during your training.

Please note: Our race insurance for this event does not permit dogs, except for service animals. If your dog is a service animal, they are welcome to join you. Otherwise, dogs unfortunately should not be brought on the race course. They are welcome to spectate with you if they are leashed, comfortable in crowds and non-reactive to other dogs. 

Post-Race

After the event, each participant will be invited to enjoy one complimentary beer (ages 21+, please bring ID if you appear under age 30), a sno-cone, plus light refreshments. 

Overall and Age Group Divisions and Awards:

Awards will be presented to the top three overall finishers per gender (male, female, nonbinary) for each the 2K, 5K, 10K, and Ten Mile.  No overall or age group awards for participants who decline to give a gender or age. Overall awards for all distances are based on gun time. Age group awards will be based on net time.  Gun time is the elapsed time from the sound of the horn to when a participant crosses the finish line. Net time is the elapsed time from when the participant crossed the start line timing mats to when they cross the finish line.

  • Age Groups for the 5K and 10K are: 9 and Under, 10-12, 13-15, 16-19, 20-24, 25-29, […], 75-79, 80-84, 85+. Note: will extend to 85-89, 90+ if participants in these categories.
  • Age Groups for the Ten Mile are: 15 and Under, 16-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70+.
  • Age Groups for the 2K are: 6 and Under, 7-9, 10-12, 13-17, 18-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69, 70+.

Special Divisions (5K, 10K, 10 Mile)

- Cancer Survivor
- Davis Resident
- Woodland Resident
- Sacramento Resident
- College Student 
  • Any 2 or 4 year undergraduate, graduate, professional, or technical degree school/program is considered eligible
  • Open to those who are currently enrolled in a program (e.g. summer school) or who will be enrolled in a program for Fall 2025
- Adaptive Division for Athletes With Disabilities
  • The Davis Moo-nlight Races encourages participation in the event by athletes with disabilities.
  • We will recognize the top 3 athletes in the adaptive division, by gender, with a special prize. 
Notes:
  • It is not possible to enter more than one special division. If you are eligible for more than one division, you will need to pick one.
  • Awards are not mailed. Check race results before you leave the event. Scan the QR code on your race bib with your phone or use one of the available chromebooks to check results.

name: Davis Stampede
description:
The Davis Stampede takes place each year in February, and includes 5K, 10K and Half Marathon routes. We also offer a family friendly 2K (1.24 mile) fun run/walk division that is perfect for younger athletes, families, and pups. Starting and finishing at Davis’ Playfields Park, the Davis Stampede is a great way to kick off 2026 with a commitment to fitness. Courses are mostly flat and take runners and walkers through east and south Davis’s greenbelts and neighborhood streets. Race amenities include finisher’s medals, half marathon pace groups, t-shirts, a post-race expo, and course water stations stocked with water and electrolyte replacement along the course.

 

Registration will open on October 1, 2025

Please register early! The Half Marathon often sells out or comes close to it.

 

Start Times:

8:00 a.m. - Half Marathon and 10K
8:10 a.m. - 5K
9:00 a.m. - 2K 
last updated 9/2025; subject to change

Entry Includes:

Blend performance short sleeved t-shirt, finisher medal, chip timing, eligibility for division awards. Option to upgrade to a long sleeve technical (100% polyester) shirt for $8; available while supplies last. You also may opt out of the short sleeve t-shirt and save $5. 

Packet Pick Up:

You can pick up your packet (bib and shirt) on Saturday, February 21 from 1pm to 4pm at Playfields Park (race venue). We allow you to pick up for friends, and ID is not required.  You can also pick up on race day (Feb. 22) starting at 6:30 a.m. If picking up on race day, we suggest arriving at least one hour prior to your race start. We encourage all participants to have their QR code available on their phone for fast check-in. You can find this in your confirmation email. 

Safety pins will be available at registration. On race morning, please pin your race bib to the clothing on the FRONT of your body so that it is visible to timing officials, course monitors, and race photographers. 

Overall and Age Group Awards:

Overall awards will be presented to the top male, female and nonbinary finishers based on gun time. Age group awards will be determined by net time and will be awarded to the top three male, female, and nonbinary registrants per age group. Registrants may decline to state their gender and / or age, however, those entrants will not be eligible for age group or overall awards or results ranking in those categories.  Award pick up is available on race day; unclaimed awards are not mailed. Awards also presented to the top three finishers in each special division. See section below for more detailed information on age groups and special divisions. 

Participate Virtually:

Those who are unable to attend on event day or who would prefer to participate on their own schedule may register as a virtual participant. Virtual packets will be mailed on or about 2/25/26 and will include a bib, finisher medal for the division you designate upon entry, and t-shirt (if selected). Virtual participants are welcome to pick up their packets at the Saturday Packet Pick Up if preferred. The deadline to sign up as a Virtual Participant is Thursday, February 19. The last day to request a switch from an in-person division to the virtual division (in cases of injury, change of plans, illness, etc.) is February 21 at 11:59 pm and this may be done via email.  Virtual participants may upload their results online by following these steps: (1) search name in upper right-hand corner; (2) next to name, click 'edit time'; (3) input your finish time in the format of HH:MM:SS and provide other requested information. Times may be submitted from February 21 through March 22 (link will be available on Feb. 21), although you may complete your run/walk any time that works for you after time of registration. Submitting a time is optional and not required. There are no age group or overall awards for the virtual divisions.  

Half Marathon:


Half Marathon course cut-off time is 3.5 hours or 11:30 a.m. Those on a pace to finish after this time will be offered a ride back to the finish line.

Minimum age to participate in the Half Marathon is 15. Consideration will be made on a case by case basis for youth 14 and under to participate in the Half Marathon who are sufficiently trained; must be accompanied by an adult (who must be registered). Send your request to acopfoundation@gmail.com by February 12th.

Water/fluid stations will be located approximately every two miles and will offer water and electrolyte replacement. Please carry nutrition or salt with you should it be a part of your training/racing regimen. 

Strollers, Wagons, and Wheels:

Wheelchair entrants may participate in all divisions. Racing wheelchairs should start at the front and coordinate with event official; pushed or casual wheelchair entrants should start toward the back. Pushed wheelchairs should start towards the back. Adaptive Divisions in the 5K, 10K, and Half Marathon.  Please note: half marathon has approximately 1/4 mile on crushed gravel by Barovetto Park plus about 1 mile on trail (service road around Wildhorse Golf Course). 5K or 10K entrants wishing to push a stroller MUST start toward the back of the pack at the starting line, no exceptions.  In the 2K, strollers and wagons (for children) and wheelchairs are permitted. Wagons must have seatbelts if children are inside them. Those with  strollers should line up behind the runners who are participating without a stroller. It is not suggested that children under age 11 run unaccompanied in the 2K. 

Timing:

Because this even utilizes chip timing for all events, we remind participants that there is no need to crowd the start line when the race starts; your time does not start until you physically cross the mats at the starting line. All age group awards and results placements, except for the top overall finishers (i.e. first 3 per gender across the finish line), are determined by chip/net time.

Guides/Support Runners for Adaptive Entrants:

If you are a sighted guide for a visually impaired participant, or a support runner/walker for an entrant in an adaptive category, please do not enter the adaptive division. Support Runners (including sighted guides) must be registered for the event either as a standard paid entrant or as a support runner. To register for the support runner/walker category, select "Support Runner" choice at registration (end of list). Those registering as a support runner will not be eligible for age group awards nor be ranked by age.   In the case that support runners  wish to receive the full race experience (eligible for awards, ranked by age division, etc) in that case they should register for the distance they are going to run/walk (Half Marathon, 5K, etc) instead of as a Support Runner, but be sure to not enter an Adaptive Division. 8:10 a.m. - 5K
9:00 a.m. - 2K

Packet Pick Up:

You can pick up your packet (bib and shirt) on Saturday, February 21 from 1pm to 4pm at Playfields Park (race venue). Overall and Age Group Awards:

Participate Virtually:

Half Marathon:

Adaptive Divisions in the 5K, 10K, and Half Marathon.  Please note: half marathon has approximately 1/4 mile on crushed gravel by Barovetto Park plus about 1 mile on trail (service road around Wildhorse Golf Course). 5K or 10K entrants wishing to push a stroller MUST start toward the back of the pack at the starting line, no exceptions.  In the 2K, strollers and wagons (for children) and wheelchairs are permitted. It is not suggested that children under age 11 run unaccompanied in the 2K.

name: Davis Stampede
description:
The Davis Stampede takes place each year in February, and includes 5K, 10K and Half Marathon routes. We also offer a family friendly 2K (1.24 mile) fun run/walk division that is perfect for younger athletes, families, and pups. Starting and finishing at Davis’ Playfields Park, the Davis Stampede is a great way to kick off 2026 with a commitment to fitness. Courses are mostly flat and take runners and walkers through east and south Davis’s greenbelts and neighborhood streets. Race amenities include finisher’s medals, half marathon pace groups, t-shirts, a post-race expo, and course water stations stocked with water and electrolyte replacement along the course.

 

Registration will open on October 1, 2025

Please register early! The Half Marathon often sells out or comes close to it.

 

Start Times:

8:00 a.m. - Half Marathon and 10K
8:10 a.m. - 5K
9:00 a.m. - 2K 
last updated 9/2025; subject to change

Entry Includes:

Blend performance short sleeved t-shirt, finisher medal, chip timing, eligibility for division awards. Option to upgrade to a long sleeve technical (100% polyester) shirt for $8; available while supplies last. You also may opt out of the short sleeve t-shirt and save $5. 

Packet Pick Up:

You can pick up your packet (bib and shirt) on Saturday, February 21 from 1pm to 4pm at Playfields Park (race venue). We allow you to pick up for friends, and ID is not required.  You can also pick up on race day (Feb. 22) starting at 6:30 a.m. If picking up on race day, we suggest arriving at least one hour prior to your race start. We encourage all participants to have their QR code available on their phone for fast check-in. You can find this in your confirmation email. 

Safety pins will be available at registration. On race morning, please pin your race bib to the clothing on the FRONT of your body so that it is visible to timing officials, course monitors, and race photographers. 

Overall and Age Group Awards:

Overall awards will be presented to the top male, female and nonbinary finishers based on gun time. Age group awards will be determined by net time and will be awarded to the top three male, female, and nonbinary registrants per age group. Registrants may decline to state their gender and / or age, however, those entrants will not be eligible for age group or overall awards or results ranking in those categories.  Award pick up is available on race day; unclaimed awards are not mailed. Awards also presented to the top three finishers in each special division. See section below for more detailed information on age groups and special divisions. 

Participate Virtually:

Those who are unable to attend on event day or who would prefer to participate on their own schedule may register as a virtual participant. Virtual packets will be mailed on or about 2/25/26 and will include a bib, finisher medal for the division you designate upon entry, and t-shirt (if selected). Virtual participants are welcome to pick up their packets at the Saturday Packet Pick Up if preferred. The deadline to sign up as a Virtual Participant is Thursday, February 19. The last day to request a switch from an in-person division to the virtual division (in cases of injury, change of plans, illness, etc.) is February 21 at 11:59 pm and this may be done via email.  Virtual participants may upload their results online by following these steps: (1) search name in upper right-hand corner; (2) next to name, click 'edit time'; (3) input your finish time in the format of HH:MM:SS and provide other requested information. Times may be submitted from February 21 through March 22 (link will be available on Feb. 21), although you may complete your run/walk any time that works for you after time of registration. Submitting a time is optional and not required. There are no age group or overall awards for the virtual divisions.  

Half Marathon:


Half Marathon course cut-off time is 3.5 hours or 11:30 a.m. Those on a pace to finish after this time will be offered a ride back to the finish line.

Minimum age to participate in the Half Marathon is 15. Consideration will be made on a case by case basis for youth 14 and under to participate in the Half Marathon who are sufficiently trained; must be accompanied by an adult (who must be registered). Send your request to acopfoundation@gmail.com by February 12th.

Water/fluid stations will be located approximately every two miles and will offer water and electrolyte replacement. Please carry nutrition or salt with you should it be a part of your training/racing regimen. 

Strollers, Wagons, and Wheels:

Wheelchair entrants may participate in all divisions. Racing wheelchairs should start at the front and coordinate with event official; pushed or casual wheelchair entrants should start toward the back. Pushed wheelchairs should start towards the back. Adaptive Divisions in the 5K, 10K, and Half Marathon.  Please note: half marathon has approximately 1/4 mile on crushed gravel by Barovetto Park plus about 1 mile on trail (service road around Wildhorse Golf Course). 5K or 10K entrants wishing to push a stroller MUST start toward the back of the pack at the starting line, no exceptions.  In the 2K, strollers and wagons (for children) and wheelchairs are permitted. Wagons must have seatbelts if children are inside them. Those with  strollers should line up behind the runners who are participating without a stroller. It is not suggested that children under age 11 run unaccompanied in the 2K. 

Timing:

Because this even utilizes chip timing for all events, we remind participants that there is no need to crowd the start line when the race starts; your time does not start until you physically cross the mats at the starting line. All age group awards and results placements, except for the top overall finishers (i.e. first 3 per gender across the finish line), are determined by chip/net time.

Guides/Support Runners for Adaptive Entrants:

If you are a sighted guide for a visually impaired participant, or a support runner/walker for an entrant in an adaptive category, please do not enter the adaptive division. Support Runners (including sighted guides) must be registered for the event either as a standard paid entrant or as a support runner. To register for the support runner/walker category, select "Support Runner" choice at registration (end of list). Those registering as a support runner will not be eligible for age group awards nor be ranked by age.   In the case that support runners  wish to receive the full race experience (eligible for awards, ranked by age division, etc) in that case they should register for the distance they are going to run/walk (Half Marathon, 5K, etc) instead of as a Support Runner, but be sure to not enter an Adaptive Division. Email acopfoundation@gmail.com with any questions prior to registering.  

Notes:

- Please do not register as a Support Runner if you do not already have an athlete you are paired with. At this time we do not have a matching program, but will post if there are adaptive entrants seeking support runners.

name: Davis Stampede Vendor Registration
description:
This is a vendor registration page for the 2025 Davis Stampede, taking place on Sunday, February 23, 2025 at Playfields Park. Vendor booths are 10' by 10'. Tents, tables, tablecloths and other items to be supplied by vendor. A site map and one-sheet will be emailed out on approximately February 18.

Set up & Timeframe:

All set up takes place on race morning from 5:45 to 6:45 a.m. Expect clean up to begin at approximately 11:45 a.m.

Vendor Parking:

A limited amount of vendor parking is available in the parking lot where the expo takes place. We suggest arriving by 6:30 am to procure a space. Vendors are not able to drive up to their booths to unload, however, the walk is fairly short from the available lot spaces to the booth area.

Expected Participation:

Approximately 500 half marathoners and 1,800 2K/5K/10K participants.

name: Day of The Dead 5K & 10k
description:
Event Location

  • Date & Time: Sunday, October 25, 2026
    Location: Wild Runners Fair Oaks, 10149 Fair Oaks Blvd, Fair Oaks, CA

Participant Packet Pick Up

  • Saturday, October 24, 2026, 10 am – 4 pm
  • Race Day, Sunday, October 25, 2026, 6:30am - 7:30 am
  • Location: Wild Runners Fair Oaks, 10149 Fair Oaks Blvd,  Fair Oaks Ca 95628

Race Day Schedule

  • 6:30 am - 7:30 am: Race day registration and packet pick up
  • 7:30 am: All final items dropped off for the La Ofrenda
  • 8:05 am - Kids Races begin
  • 8:20 am - Day of the Dead progression to starting line
  • 8:30 am - Day of the Dead 5k/10k race begins
  • 9:30 am - Awards ceremony and costume contest

Swag & Event

All participants receive:

  • Bib number, timing device and safety pins
  • Short-sleeved event shirt
  • Finisher medal
  • Coupon for one-free tamale for each participant*
  • Special offers from our sponsors

* Redeemable only at the post-event expo and festival on October 25, 2026. 

  • Family-Friendly Walk/Run Events: The Day of the Dead 5k has something for every generation to enjoy from a 5k for adults to our Kid Races. 
    Live Entertainment: Immerse yourself in Mexican tradition with live music and performances. With stilt walkers and live music, transport yourself to another time as we pay homage to the cultural heritage of our grandparents.
  • La Ofrenda: To honor loved ones who have passed, bring offerings, such as photographs, flowers, nostalgic items, and foods as we create a collective space of remembrance and gratitude.  All items should be placed on La Ofrenda by 7:30am in front of the Wild Runners store at 10149 Fair Oaks Blvd.
  • Antojitos Delights: Enjoy the flavors and culinary delights that our grandparents cherished. In addition to free home-made tamales for race participants, indulge in the food and delectable treats of Mexican heritage.
  • Post-Race Festival and Expo: Unwind and connect with fellow participants post race! Explore our Community Partner and vendor booths showcasing the latest in fitness, wellness, and recovery services.  

5k Course

The race kicks off with a 0.5-mile downhill through the charming Old Fair Oaks Village neighborhood and over the bridge. Following a 3.2-mile out-and-back path along the picturesque American River Trail towards Bannister Park, the course remains entirely on paved roads and trails, catering to participants of all abilities and those with strollers.  The race concludes with an approximate half-mile ascent back to the finish line.

Awards & Age Divisions

Awards ceremony to follow event at 9:30 a.m. for the 5k and costume contest. Prizes for overall male and female winners will be presented. Top three finishers in each age division will receive a special prize. Age-group winners pick up prizes at the Awards table.

Top boy and girl finishers in the 1/4 and 1/2 mile races will receive a special prize. All other kid finishers will receive medals.

Top 3 finishers in the male and female races will respectively receive: 

  • 1st Place: $100 gift card to Wild Runners
  • 2nd Place: $50 gift card to Wild Runners
  • 3rd Place: $25 gift card to Wild Runners

1st place finishers in each Age Group (5k Run) will receive a free pair of socks from our sponsor from OS1st:
12 & Under, 13-15, 16-18, 19-24, 25-29, 30-34, 35-39, 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, 80+

Costume Contest:

  • 1st Place: $100 gift card to Wild Runners
  • 2nd Place: $50 gift card to Wild Runners
  • 3rd Place: $25 gift card to Wild Runners

Rules & Guidelines for all entrants*

  • Bib numbers must not be altered, should be worn on the front of the runner, and be visible.
  • No unregistered runners, walkers or pacers.
  • Wearing headphones is discouraged.
  • No bicycles.
  • Your pup is welcome to participate in the 5k race (always on leash and after signing a waiver).
  • Strollers are welcome.
  • Walkers/runners of all abilities and capabilities welcome. 
  • Shirts are not guaranteed for the late registration ( you can ask for previos year shirt)

* No refunds

name: Desert Orienteering Festival
description:
Please consider volunteering. All volunteers will receive an email with a $50 coupon toward registration per slot. 

REMINDER: DOF26 will not be offering OUSA categories. Run any race you want! 

***************************************************************************************************************

Saturday, Jan 17th

The Adventure Trek

12pm Mass Start

The festival kicks off with a 2-hour score orienteering Adventure Trek, where both experienced and beginner participants can chart their own path through the desert.

This year’s challenge takes place in the vast flatlands northeast of Buttes Pass, where navigational precision and overland speed will be the keys to victory.

Course Setter: Chris Day

 

Sunday, Jan 18th

The Classic

Starts 10am-11:30am

Measure your fitness and navigation skills against the best in a traditional 7-course classic orienteering competition that will span both technical and fast terrain.

Beginners can stick to the basic White course or use their newly built skills to take on the Yellow or Orange competitions.

Course Setter:  Matej Sebo

 

The Night Goat

5pm Mass Start

Are you ready to take on the desert at night? ​

This modified format will extend our Goat (8-10km), Borrego (4-5km), and Beginner mass start tradition, but with a dusk start time. Following is encouraged, but as night settles and the group splinters, you might face the dark desert alone to complete this point-to-point course. Beginners who want just a taste of the night can opt for a lighted guide.

Course Setter:  Mark Prior

 

Monday, Jan 19th

The Maze Middle

Starts 9am-11am

Navigate the slot canyons and steep slopes of the iconic "Maze" in a middle distance 7-course point to point competition. The distances will be short, but the complexity high, with numerous route options and physical challenges between controls in this three-dimensional wonderland.

Beginners will thrill to exposed ridges and memorable vistas while following a more straight-forward route. 

Course Setter: Julien Ouellet

The Run/Walk 4 Kids is a fun filled, family and pet friendly event. Admission into the event is free with a minimal donation requested to participate in the 5K. The Family Bubble Run will kick off immediately after completion of the 5K.

Why We Walk - Until we achieve a cure, our efforts will ensure these families receive the comfort, relief, support and fun to help them in the ultimate fight against these diseases. Please join our foundations in the fight to CURE Pediatric Cancer and other serious illnesses.

The Desi Strong Foundation is geared to help children facing cancer feel that love & support that Desi was so graciously granted. Together we will fight this beast called Childhood Cancer & help fund for a cure.

We can’t all be doctors or cancer researchers or caregivers but walking with us can raise the money that makes their work possible. And in the meantime, help children and their families feel the love while they fight these horrible diseases.

There are various levels of sponsorship available for the 5K and Kids Fun Run. As you will see, each sponsor will be highly visible in many aspects of the event. We hope that you will consider sponsoring our race.

name: Día de  Muertos - Viva la Vida - 5K, 10K, and Half Marathon by Califlow Runs
description:
🌺 Viva La Vida 5K, 10K & Half Marathon
📅 Sunday, November 2 | Long Beach, CA
📍 Start/Finish: 5400 E Ocean Blvd

💀 Celebrate life, honor those who came before us, and run your heart out at our Day of the Dead-inspired race by the beach. Dress to impress—our costume contest is ON! Whether you're decked out in marigolds, skull face paint, or a full-on altar on your back (hey, we’ve seen it all), this run is about honoring traditions and having a blast.

 

🏁 Race Day Schedule:

Two Start Times for the different distances 

Half Marathon: 7:00 AM
5K & 10K: 8:00 AM
Bib Pick-Up (Runner Check in): 6:15–8:00 AM @ the Race Ready Athletics Tent
Course Cut-Off: 10:30 AM sharp


🎉 Event Highlights:

🏅 Viva la VidaFinisher Medals
📸 Free Race-Day Photos
⏱️ Chip-Timed with Awards
🚰 Water Stations & Restrooms on Course
👶 Stroller-Friendly, Beginner-Welcoming
🍩 Epic Photo Stops 
🎭 Costume Contest Prizes


🌞 Why CaliFlow Runs?
We're not just a race—we're a movement. Expect high vibes, community spirit, and themes that make you say "Wait, what?!" Whether you're chasing a PR or just vibing in your skeleton jumpsuit, you belong here.

name: Dia De Los Reyes Magos Half Marathon & 5k - Bakersfield
description:
"Dia de los Reyes Magos" or 3 wise men day is a very important Mexican celebration! On January 6th, kids are expected to receive presents from the "Reyes Magos" and families get together to share the "Rosca de Reyes" or sweet bread and drink some hot chocolate! This "Rosca de Reyes" bread contains inside several baby Jesus. It's the tradition that whoever gets the baby Jesus is expected to bring tamales and hot chocolate on February 2nd! Join us at this celebration for a morning of family fun at the Dia De Los Reyes Magos Half Marathon and 5k. 

A few reasons to join our event:

  • UNIQUE MEDALS
  • AGE GROUP UNIQUE AWARDS FOR BOTH 5K AND HALF MARATHON
  • HOODIES (FOR THOSE WHO REGISTER BEFORE DECEMBER 15TH) SHIRTS FOR THOSE WHO SIGN UP AFTER
  • TACOS
  • HOT CHOCOLATE
  • $100 TO FIRST MALE/FEMALE IN THE HALF MARATHON
  • ROSCA DE REYES SWEET BREAD
  • FLAT, PAVED, OUT AND BACK FAST COURSE
  • ATHENA, CLYDESDALE CATEGORIES/AGE GROUP AWARDS
  • KIDS RACES
  • FOLKLORICO
  • MUSIC

RACE LOCATION: YOKUTS PARK, 4200 EMPIRE DR, BAKERSFIELD, CALIFORNIA, 93309

BIB PICK UP ONLY ON RACE DAY: 6:45-8:45AM @ YOKUTS PARK 

HALF MARATHON START TIME: 8:00AM

KIDS RACES START TIME: 8:45AM

5K RACE START TIME: 9:00AM

NO AWARDS/MEDAL WILL BE MAILED AFTER THE EVENT. PLEASE CHECK RESULTS ON RACE DAY AND MAKE SURE YOU TAKE YOUR AWARD IF YOU GOT ONE.

name: Do It For Her 5K
description:
Run through Temecula’s Wine Country and enjoy the tranquil beauty of rolling vineyards and sun-drenched hills. As you run along the winding paths, the early morning light casts a golden hue over the landscape, highlighting the neat rows of grapevines and the rustic charm of the wineries scattered throughout the valley. Finish with a Vitagliano sangria made from some of the finest Super Tuscan-style wines produced in California.  Shop our local vendors carrying locally grown produce and handcrafted items, all under a beautiful covered patio.  Food Available for purchase.


All proceeds benefit the Heather Janikowski Foundation and the Make A Wish Foundation

description:
Join us for the 'Run for Paws: DoggieRun 4K/5K' event! This fun and family-friendly race celebrates our furry friends and promotes healthy, active lifestyles for both humans and their canine companions. name: Don Osborne Memorial Run
description:

This event will happen rain or shine. Light snacks, fruit, juice, and water will be available for all participants.

  • What: 5k Run and 1 Mile Run/Walk on the flat, paved city streets with traffic control

name: Dream Big 5k
description:
Join us for a day of fun and fitness at the third annual Dream Big 5k, proudly presented by the Kiwanis Club of Victorville. Whether you’re a seasoned runner or just looking for a fun walk with friends and family, this event promises an enjoyable experience for participants of all levels.

The race takes you through the scenic paths of Victor Valley College, located at 18422 Bear Valley Rd, Victorville, CA, starting bright and early at 8:00 am on Saturday, August 22. But the fun doesn't end at the finish line! Stick around for a variety of race day activities, including local vendors, lively music, and more. Every stride you take helps us support students in the Victor Valley, driving the change we wish to see in our community. Grab your running shoes, and let’s make dreams come true together at the Dream Big 5k!

After the main Dream Big 5K, stick around for even more fun—our Dream Big Mini K for children ages 12 and under! Held at Victor Valley College, this in-person event is all about encouraging kids to get active, dream big, and feel proud of their accomplishments. It’s a joyful, high-energy experience where little ones can cross the finish line to the cheers of friends and family.

The first 50 registered participants of the Mini K will receive a special finisher medal—so don’t wait to sign up! Let’s make it a day to remember filled with smiles, movement, and celebration. Come cheer them on and help create a lasting memory at the Dream Big Mini K!

name: Elevate 5k & 12 Hour Race at First Baptist Church
description:
Please visit www.ElevateRace.com for the most up to date and detailed information.
Thank you for your interest in participating in our 8th annual Elevate race!

  • What: 5k & 12 hour race
  • Purpose: To support our Elevate missions project
  • When: 5k starts Sat, Feb 14, 2026 @ 9:30am / 12 hour race starts Fri, Feb 13, 2026 @ 8:45pm
  • Where: First Baptist Church campus in Santa Maria, CA
  • Cost:
    • 5k = $22
    • 12 Hour = $45 (This is a bargain! The average price for 12 hour races here in CA is $155.)


All the proceeds from this event will go to support the Elevate missions project. Your participation as either a runner or volunteer will help make it possible!

5k: For only $22 you can challenge yourself to complete the 5k (3.1 miles) race. Awards will be given to the winners in both distances for the different age groups at the 10:30am awards ceremony. While this is a competition, everyone is invited to participate regardless of age or physical ability. It will be a lively and encouraging environment which will be fun for both first timers and experienced runners. Runners must arrive by 8:45 on race morning to receive their race bib and all final instructions before the race begins at 9:30am.  The 5k awards ceremony will take place at 10:30am.

12 Hour race: I know we have some adventurous people out there! How far do you think you could run and walk in 12 hours? The race runs from Friday night at 8:45pm until Saturday morning at 8:45am. It will finish 45 minutes before the start of the 5k. This is a great time to test yourself physically and mentally. Would you like to complete your first marathon? In 12 hours you could even walk a marathon if you could finish each mile in just under 28 minutes.

Here's some good news. We'll have some food and drinks to fuel you through the night, and you can take breaks as often as you'd like. Each lap is 1 mile, and near the start/finish line we'll have an area set up specifically for the 12 hour participants. You're encouraged to bring a comfortable chair, footrest, change of clothes, blankets and anything else that can help make your experience more comfortable. Napping is permitted but not encouraged. Friends and family members are invited to spend the evening there with us supporting and encouraging the participants. There is no minimum number of miles you have to complete. Yes, the person that completes the most loops is the winner, but runners and walkers of all levels are encouraged to set an individual goal and see what they're capable of doing. Races like this are typically very relaxed. Very few people would run the entire time in a race of this distance. Going through the night also provides a unique experience. There will be a variety of awards for the 12 hour race & the 12 hour race awards ceremony will take place at 8:45am right when the race finishes.

As a bonus (or maybe more like a penalty), all 12 Hour participants can also participate in the 5k for free if desired! 12 Hour runners must arrive by 8:00pm Friday evening to receive their race bib and all final instructions before the race begins at 8:45pm.

Course info: Each loop is 1.036 miles for the 5k. The 5k is three loops. For the 12 Hour race there is a minor adjustment to make each loop 1 mile. The loop is entirely on the First Baptist / VCA campus, and during the 5k there will be volunteers throughout the course in order to provide a safe environment for young runners. 12 Hour runners will need to have either a headlamp or flashlight to use on the back portion of the loop where there are no lights.

For the 5k we will have water, Gatorade and bananas during the race and celebratory ice cream sandwiches at the end for all finishers. The 12 Hour participants will have a variety of hot and cold drinks and solid foods to choose from. We hope you have a great time training for and participating in this race!

Please visit www.ElevateRace.com for the most up to date and detailed information.

5k: For only $22 you can challenge yourself to complete the 5k (3.1 miles) race. Awards will be given to the winners in both distances for the different age groups at the 10:30am awards ceremony. While this is a competition, everyone is invited to participate regardless of age or physical ability. It will be a lively and encouraging environment which will be fun for both first timers and experienced runners. Runners must arrive by 8:45 on race morning to receive their race bib and all final instructions before the race begins at 9:30am.  The 5k awards ceremony will take place at 10:30am.

12 Hour race: I know we have some adventurous people out there! How far do you think you could run and walk in 12 hours? The race runs from Friday night at 8:45pm until Saturday morning at 8:45am. It will finish 45 minutes before the start of the 5k. This is a great time to test yourself physically and mentally. Would you like to complete your first marathon? In 12 hours you could even walk a marathon if you could finish each mile in just under 28 minutes.

Here's some good news. We'll have some food and drinks to fuel you through the night, and you can take breaks as often as you'd like. Each lap is 1 mile, and near the start/finish line we'll have an area set up specifically for the 12 hour participants. You're encouraged to bring a comfortable chair, footrest, change of clothes, blankets and anything else that can help make your experience more comfortable. Napping is permitted but not encouraged. Friends and family members are invited to spend the evening there with us supporting and encouraging the participants. There is no minimum number of miles you have to complete. Yes, the person that completes the most loops is the winner, but runners and walkers of all levels are encouraged to set an individual goal and see what they're capable of doing. Races like this are typically very relaxed. Very few people would run the entire time in a race of this distance. Going through the night also provides a unique experience. There will be a variety of awards for the 12 hour race & the 12 hour race awards ceremony will take place at 8:45am right when the race finishes.

As a bonus (or maybe more like a penalty), all 12 Hour participants can also participate in the 5k for free if desired! 12 Hour runners must arrive by 8:00pm Friday evening to receive their race bib and all final instructions before the race begins at 8:45pm.

Course info: Each loop is 1.036 miles for the 5k. The 5k is three loops. For the 12 Hour race there is a minor adjustment to make each loop 1 mile. The loop is entirely on the First Baptist / VCA campus, and during the 5k there will be volunteers throughout the course in order to provide a safe environment for young runners. 12 Hour runners will need to have either a headlamp or flashlight to use on the back portion of the loop where there are no lights.

For the 5k we will have water, Gatorade and bananas during the race and celebratory ice cream sandwiches at the end for all finishers. The 12 Hour participants will have a variety of hot and cold drinks and solid foods to choose from. We hope you have a great time training for and participating in this race!

Please visit www.ElevateRace.com for the most up to date and detailed information.

name: Ely Mountain Trail Race
description:
Ely Mountain Trail Race – Shaver Lake, CA

14K (8.7mi) + 8K (4.9mi) | Balsam Forebay | Cooler temps. Hot trails.


We’re stoked to bring a brand new adventure to the San Joaquin Running Co lineup — and this one’s a beauty. Join us in the mountains above Shaver Lake for the first-ever Ely Mountain Trail Race, where crisp air, big climbs, and epic views are all on the menu.

 

The 14K course brings the heat with about 1,800 feet of climbing, including a 1,000’ ascent up Ely Mountain. You’ll earn sweeping views of the Sierra, Shaver Lake, and the valley below — then fly down some smooth and fast singletrack and dirt roads back to the finish.

 

The 8K hits a slightly easier route to the top but still climbs about 800 feet, with all the mountain vibes and finish line feels.

 

🏔️ Special Award for King & Queen of the Mountain – fastest segment times to the top of Ely!

🎽 Custom race shirts

🏅 Finisher medals + podium awards

🍕 Post-race food + refreshments

🌲 All the crisp mountain air you’ve been missing

We’re capping this one at 250 runners, so don’t sleep on it — grab your spot and come break in these trails with us.

name: End of the Trail Half Marathon, 10K & 5K
description:
PACKET PICK-UP:

February 27th (Friday). Sole 2 Soul Sports - Visalia at 4241 S. Mooney Blvd (Target Shopping Center). 

TIME: 3:00pm to 6:00pm

 

RACE DAY PACKET PICK-UP:

OPENS at 7:00am, Near the start line under the Visalia Runners Canopy

 

ALL RACES START TIME: 8:00 AM

 

START & FINISH: MOONEY GROVE PARK at the END OF THE TRAIL STATUE.

COURSE DETAILS: The half marathon, 10K, and 5K will Start & Finish at the End of the Trail Statue (road) and will run approximately 1 mile through scenic Mooney Grove Park before heading out the back gate.  The half and 10K continues out on country roads with lots of local cross country teams cheering you on. There will be  DJ Music at the 10k Turn-Around.

These routes are FLAT & FAST with closed roads, DJ’s, live bands, portable restrooms, aid stations, and more! 

At the Finish Line, you will be welcomed back with your EOTT Custom Finisher’s Medal, Hot Breakfast, Chocolate Milk, and a Post-Race Celebration in the Park! You’ll want to stay around and relax in the park with your running buddies!

Whether you Run or Walk, you'll want to join this memorable experience in the beautiful setting of Mooney Grove Park.

Race Proceeds & All Donations will benefit many local high school running programs in Tulare County, athlete scholarships and other community running events to promote health and wellness. You will see those high school runners cheering you on, working our Aid Stations, and keeping you moving!

Why End of the Trail?

  • Courses are Flat & Fast
  • It's a Post Race Party in the Park
  • Closed Running Streets
  • Perfect Cool Weather
  • Custom Finisher's Medal
  • FREE Race Tech Shirt to ALL 5K, 10K & Half Marathon participants

  • Post Race Celebration Venue for You, Family, Friends
  • And MORE

name: Endless Summer in the LBC 5K, 10K, & Half Marathon by Califlow Runs
description:
🌊☀️ Sun. Sand. Miles. Vibes. ☀️🌊

 

Join us on July 12th, 2025, for Endless Summer in the LBC, the ultimate mid-summer running experience along the beautiful Long Beach waterfront. Whether you're looking to set a new PR, enjoy a scenic run, or just soak in the summer vibes, this event has something for everyone!

🏝 Event Highlights:
✅ Scenic Course: Breathe in the fresh ocean air and enjoy stunning beach views along our fast, flat course.
✅ Frozen Treats at the Finish: Cool down with ice-cold frozen pops after you cross the finish line!
✅ Hydration Stations with ICE: Stay refreshed with Gatorade, water, and ice at two aid stations along the course.
✅ Volunteer Medic on Scooter: Keeping an eye on everyone and making sure we all stay safe in the summer heat!
✅ Beach-Themed Photo Ops: Snap your best summer vibes with our amazing beach-inspired backdrops!
✅ Shaded Family Viewing Area: Friends and family can chill in a shaded spectator zone while they cheer you on!
✅ Awards & Swag:
🏅 All finishers receive a custom medal.
📸 FREE race photos to capture the moment.
🥇 Top 3 male & female finishers in each distance win awards.

👟 Event Details:
📅 Date: Saturday, July 12, 2025
📍 Location: Long Beach Waterfront
🏃 Distances: 5K, 10K, and Half Marathon
⏰ Start Times:

7:00 AM – Half Marathon
7:30 AM – 5K & 10K
🎉 Fun Contest – Summer Vibes Edition!
Bring out your best summer-themed outfits! Show up in your most colorful, beachy, tropical attire, and you could win a special prize! Categories include:
🌴 Best Beach Bum Look
🌺 Most Tropical Vibes
😎 Coolest Sunglasses Style

📍 Race Logistics:
🎟 Bib Pick-Up: 6:15 AM – 7:35 AM at the Race Ready Athletics Tent.
🚗 Parking:

Free street parking on along Ocean Blvd.
Paid parking inside the lot $2.00 per hour.


🚻 Restrooms: Available at the start/finish area and along the course.
🍼 Stroller & Walker-Friendly: Everyone is welcome!
Why CaliFlow Runs?
We’re all about good vibes, community, and making running fun. Whether you’re a seasoned racer or just getting started, our events are designed to be inclusive, energetic, and unforgettable.

So grab your sunnies, lace up, and let’s chase Endless Summer in the LBC! 🌞🏃‍♂️🏖

name: EVERYTHING HURTS AND I'M DYING 5K/10K!
description:
NEW YEAR. STILL YOU. JUST SHOWING UP ANYWAY.

The EVERYTHING HURTS AND I'M DYING 5K/10K perfectly captures that magical moment when the calendar resets, but your muscles absolutely do not. Whether you’re easing back into movement, shaking off last year, or running purely out of spite for your couch, this run celebrates progress over pace and laughter over limits. 

Sign up for the EVERYTHING HURTS AND I'M DYING 5K/10K, complete it anytime and anywhere, and help give back to a great cause! Every entry gets you a custom high-quality shirt that is sure to be your new favorite, a cool finisher medal, along with a donation to Stand Up To Cancer in order to help SU2C get one step closer to its mission of making everyone diagnosed with cancer a survivor! 

 

TO JOIN: 

  • Register for the EVERYTHING HURTS & I'M DYING 5K/10K before March 31st, 2026
  • Complete a 5K (3.1 miles) or 10K (6.2 miles) at your convenience any time anywhere (no deadline)!
  • Celebrate your accomplishment by sharing on social media! #EverythingHurtsAndImDying #IRun4Movement

name: Face In Water Endurance Multisport Challenge 2026
description:
Face In Water, a non-profit providing customized swimming and water safety education to reduce drownings and create awareness about the importance of learning how to swim, is hosting this annual Endurance Multisport Challenge. If you exercise on purpose, you are an athlete, and we invite athletes of all ages and abilities to participate and support the Face In Water mission. This event is a virtual event, so you can participate wherever you are in the world, including your local pool or open water.

For the swim-only categories, you can choose to complete 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500 or 1,000 miles in the calendar year.

In the Multisport categories, you can swim, bike/spin, run, walk, or hike to reach your year goal. This year, we are including options for 500, 1,000 miles, 2,500 miles or 5,000 miles total of these categories. 

Distance will be tracked one of two ways:

1) If you have a Garmin device, you will be able to join a Garmin Group via invite, that is available through the Garmin Connect App. A link will be e-mailed to you once you register for the event.

2) Alternately, you have the option to track how you wish and submit via RunSignUp.

Once completed, a Face In Water branded item and finisher certificate - as well as bragging rights - will be awarded to all that complete their challenge.

All participants must turn in their distances completed to fiwracedirector@gmail.com by January 10, 2027 to receive their award.

name: Face In Water Endurance Multisport Challenge 2026
description:
Face In Water, a non-profit providing customized swimming and water safety education to reduce drownings and create awareness about the importance of learning how to swim, is hosting this annual Endurance Multisport Challenge. If you exercise on purpose, you are an athlete, and we invite athletes of all ages and abilities to participate and support the Face In Water mission. This event is a virtual event, so you can participate wherever you are in the world, including your local pool or open water.

For the swim-only categories, you can choose to complete 50, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500 or 1,000 miles in the calendar year.

In the Multisport categories, you can swim, bike/spin, run, walk, or hike to reach your year goal. This year, we are including options for 500, 1,000 miles, 2,500 miles or 5,000 miles total of these categories. 

Distance will be tracked one of two ways:

name: Father’s Day Classic – 5K, 10K, 10-Miler, and Half Marathon
description:
Celebrate Father's Day outside at the beach! Join us for our Father's Day Classic, where you can run, jog or walk with or in celebration of your dad, husband, grandpa, or any father figure in your life!

Race Details

Start Location: Long Beach Location TBD
Parking: Parking in the lot is $2/hour and starts at 8am, if you are running the Half/10m you can use the Passport app to pay for parking. Street parking is free.

Event Schedule

6:20am – Bib pick-up opens at the tables closest to Claremont Ave
7:00am – Half marathon & 10m start
7:30am – 5k & 10k start
7:35am – Registration & start line close
10:20am – Course closes (3 hours, 20 minutes for the Half and 10m)

Early start of 6:30am may be pre-arranged for half marathoners, email your request to events@hightideruns.com. All early starters will not be eligible for awards.

Out and Back Course

5k & 10k: The 5k route is used for the 5k (one lap) and 10k (two laps) – 5k route
10m: The 5m route is used for the 10m (two laps) – 5m route
Half: The 5m route is run twice and the 5k route is run once for the Half – 5m route and 5k route

More about the Course

The beach path is an open course, so you will encounter others using it. When we start the race, please stay on the right side of the beach path. The right side is for pedestrians and the left side is for cyclists.

On-Course Support: A fully stocked water station is located at the Belmont Pier. The finish line will also have an aid station stocked with water, gatorade, gels, and fruit snacks. We have a first aid kit at each station and all High Tides Crew Members have received CPR training. The turns are clearly marked with chalk, a runner turn sign, and a flag

Final Details

Bib: Please wear your race bib on the front of your shirt so we can track your time and send your pics!
Gear Check: You may leave personal items with staff at the registration tent. Please bring your own bag.
Awards: 1st place medals are given to the overall 1st male and female in each distance.
Results & Photos: An email with race results and photos will be sent the day after the race and earlier on Instagram. Race photos are free!

Join Us Again: Did you have a blast running with us at our low-pressure, high vibes race? We have themed races throughout the year in Long Beach, the San Fernando Valley, San Diego, and Orange County. Register for multiple races at a time to earn a discount. Check our full schedule

Have Another Question? Check our FAQ page, it's probably answered there!

name: Field N Dale 6K & 12K Trail Run Panorama Vista Preserve
description:
Join us for this unique and exciting trail run through the Preserve.

 

WHY RUN THE FIELD N DALE:

  • Chip Timed Race
  • 6K course is FLAT & FAST! Mainly compacted dirt & some asphalt, running along both sides of the mighty Kern River.
  • 12K course is a Challenging Trail Run, which climbs the bluffs and a portion follows single track trails.
  • Unique & Hand-Made Top 3 Age Group Awards, that you ONLY can get from the Preserve.
  • Custom event t-shirt
  • FREE Post Race Pancakes Breakfast (sponsored by The Boy Scouts of America)
  • Post Race Raffles
  • Awesome Finisher's Medal

ABOUT THE PANORAMA VISTA PRESERVE:

The Panorama Vista Preserve is located on both sides of the Kern River. Through its re-vegetation projects, it is increasingly an oasis where people come to enjoy a bit of tranquility. Here, they escape urban hub-bub and enjoy sounds and sights of nature. Oildale is to the west and Gordon's Ferry to the east, the Beardsley Canal and oil fields to the north, and the historic Panorama Bluffs to the south. The Preserve is private land held in trust for the public; it's owner is the Kern River Corridor Endowment and Holding Co. (KRCE), a non-profit 501(3)(c) entity; its Board of Directors are unpaid volunteers.

It is open to the public for gentle use and is in this way a gift to the community.

name: Finish The Ride and Finish The Run Santa Clarita
description:
Finish The Ride & Finish The Run – Santa Clarita
Sunday, October 25, 2026 • 6:00 AM – 2:00 PM
West Creek Park • 24247 Village Circle Drive, Valencia, CA 91354

Join us for a memorable day of running, riding, walking, and rolling—all for a purpose. Finish The Ride & Finish The Run is more than an event; it’s a movement to make roads safer for cyclists, pedestrians, and drivers everywhere.

 
🌄 What to Expect


Multiple Ride Options (Routes are subject to change)
• 12‑Mile Family Fun Ride/Roll – ideal for beginners & families (mostly on bike paths). 
• 25‑Mile Tour de River Ride – advanced beginner/intermediate route. 
• 62‑Mile Metric Century – challenging ride with scenic canyons and elevation gain (~3,500 ft).


Run/Walk Options
• 5K Run/Walk
• 10K Run/Walk
• 1K Kids & Puppy Run – for little ones and canine companions. 
 
🕒 Schedule (October 25, 2026)


Time                                             Event


6:00 AM                                       Check‑in opens
7:00 AM                                       Metric Century ride starts
8:00 AM                                       Opening Ceremony with special guest speakers
8:15 AM                                       12‑Mile Fun Ride/Roll & 25‑Mile Tour de River Ride begin
8:30 AM                                       5K & 10K Run/Walk begin
9:00 AM                                       Expo area opens; raffle drawings throughout the morning
9:30 AM                                       1K Kids & Puppy Runs begin
2:00 PM                                       Expo closes

 
✔ Important Details


Packet Pickup: Information on the location and dates of packet pickup will be posted here as soon as it becomes available, as well as sent out in event emails. Includes your bib, helmet‑sticker (for rides), route maps, & any ordered shirts/jerseys. 


Costumes: Halloween themed! Dress up if you’d like – we’ll have awards for the best costumes. 


Support & Aid: Rides are supported by marshals, sag wagons, and free repair/tune‑up stations. If you need assistance, we’re here to help. 


Water & Refreshments: Stations on route for rides & runs; snacks & food trucks at the expo. 


Age & Participation Rules:
• Children under 14 must be accompanied by parent/guardian. 
• Minimum ages vary by event: e.g. 12‑mile ride ≥ 5 yrs, 25‑mile ≥ 8 yrs, 62‑mile ≥ 15 yrs. Runs also have age minimum. 


 
🎯 Why This Matters
Finish The Ride & Finish The Run was founded by Damian Kevitt after a life‑changing hit‑and‑run. What began as one person’s effort to overcome tragedy has grown into a community movement advocating for safer streets in Southern California and beyond. By participating, you are helping raise awareness and support systemic changes—policies, education, infrastructure—that make roads safer for all through Streets Are For Everyone.

 
📍 Logistics & Registration


Location: West Creek Park, Valencia – 24247 Village Circle Drive.

Transportation: Consider taking the Metrolink (Antelope Valley Line) + connecting bus, or ride your bike from the station up to West Creek Park. Streets Are For Everyone
Fees & Discounts: Registration options vary by event. Special rates may apply for veterans, first responders, groups, etc. Contact us directly at Events@StreetsAreForEveryone.org for more information.
What’s included: Event t‑shirt or athletic sleeves with registration, finishing medals for all events, awards, expo, etc. 
 
Come ride, run, walk, roll—or cheer—on this meaningful day. Let’s finish the ride, finish the run, and finish strong for safer streets for everyone. #NeverGiveUp

name: Fleet Feet Fall Classic - Trail October 18th, 2026
description:
LOCATION

South Rim Trail Head/ Backside of Bidwell Golf Course
Chico, CA US 95928

 

DISCRIPTION 

Fleet Feet Chico is pleased to offer two trail races in our beautiful Upper Bidwell Park.  The two races will start on the south side of the park down Annies Trail for a fun adventure on the single-track trails. Toss in a creek crossing and a nice finish through Yahi and the golf course, you’re sure to enjoy your run! 

 

The two races include a half marathon and a 4-mile an hour backyard endurance challenge! 

 

The Half Marathon will start at 8:10am along the rock wall off Centennial/South Rim trail head. This race will be a challenging climb with 1600 ft of gain in the first half. Enjoy a party at the top of 10-mile house at Aid station #1 and enjoy an all downhill second half of the race!

 

4-mile endurance race will start at 8:00am. Runners will run a 4-mile loop. If you complete the loop in under 60 mins you will go back in the shoot for loop #2. At the top of each hour a new round will start. This will continue for 8 hours! Every other lap we will change the direction of the loop!  If there is more than one person going into the final hour the run will become a foot race to the finish! If you complete all 8 loops, you will have run approximately 32 Miles! Do you have what it takes? Do one loop, 3 loops or all 8! It’s sure to be a good time for the runners and the spectators!

 

After the race head up to Bidwell Golf Course Bar and grill for some delicious food and drinks! All runners get a breakfast burrito with your race registration plus and additional 15% off any other food or drink. 

 

By supporting this race, you are supporting two great causes! 

Chico Velo Trailworks. Launched in 2014, Chico Velo’s Trailworks supports and manages the creation and maintenance of sustainable and enjoyable trails in our region. They have established a strong partnership with the City of Chico to maintain the trails in Upper Bidwell Park. Trailworks have done additional work in the Oroville area and beyond. They are actively seeking new partnerships and opportunities within our community to promote sustainable trail design. Trailworks volunteers put in hundreds of hours every year improving trails for all users to enjoy. To see their latest project check out our Colby Mountain Recreation Project.  A portion of your race entry will go to this great local stewardship as they continue their work to help keep our local trails accessible for us all! If you would like more information on this program or would like to sign up for a park cleanup day, click the link below.

Chico Velo Trailworks - CHICO VELO

 

In addition to supporting Chico Velo Trailworks we are also donating a portion of the race proceeds to local fire academy cadets. Many of the current class are volunteer firefighters who have worked and volunteered in our community and are continuing their education to be able to make a lifelong career the Fire industry. With a fire prone environment that we live in throughout Butte County we rely on our local fire personnel, staff and volunteers to keep our community safe! Cadets will be volunteering on the racecourse to help ensure the safety of all our participants.  Cadets can be seen on our racecourse supporting our race as emergency EMTs and safety aids at the creek crossings. If you are interested in becoming a volunteer firefighter visit the links below for more information.

Become a Volunteer | Butte County, CA

 

RACE START TIMES


4-Mile Endurance Run            8:00am

Half Marathon                         8:10am

 

REGISTRATION

Registration for this race is available online.

  • Online registration closes October 16th at 9:00am.
  • In person registration on October 16th and 17th at Fleet Feet Chico from 10am-2pm.
  • Register by Friday September 29th to guarantee yourself race shirt.
  • If you register between September 18th – October 18th your shirt will NOT be guaranteed, they will be first come first serve at packet pickup.
  • All leftover shirts (if any) will be available for pickup or for sale (non-registered runners) AFTER the Half Marathon race on October 18th. The shirts will be available first come first serve starting at 10:00am.  

 

RACE FEE SCHEDULE

  • October 21st – December 31st - (online)        
    • Half Marathon   $80.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run     $80.00
  • January 1st – May  31st (online)         
    • Half Mar._______________$85.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run___$85.00
  • June 1st- September 30th (online)
    • Half Marathon__________$90.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run___$90.00
  • October 1st- October 16th (online, closes at 9:00am on 10.16)
    • Half Marathon__________$95.00
    • 4-Mile Endurance Run___$95.00

  • In person Registration at Packet Pickup (Oct. 16th and 17th) ONLY
    • Half Marathon__________$100.00

name: Fleet Feet Fall Classic - Trail October 18th, 2026
description:
LOCATION

South Rim Trail Head/ Backside of Bidwell Golf Course
Chico, CA US 95928

 

DISCRIPTION 

Fleet Feet Chico is pleased to offer two trail races in our beautiful Upper Bidwell Park.  The two races will start on the south side of the park down Annies Trail for a fun adventure on the single-track trails. Toss in a creek crossing and a nice finish through Yahi and the golf course, you’re sure to enjoy your run! 

 

The two races include a half marathon and a 4-mile an hour backyard endurance challenge! 

 

The Half Marathon will start at 8:10am along the rock wall off Centennial/South Rim trail head. This race will be a challenging climb with 1600 ft of gain in the first half. Enjoy a party at the top of 10-mile house at Aid station #1 and enjoy an all downhill second half of the race!

 

4-mile endurance race will start at 8:00am. Runners will run a 4-mile loop. If you complete the loop in under 60 mins you will go back in the shoot for loop #2. At the top of each hour a new round will start. This will continue for 8 hours! Every other lap we will change the direction of the loop!  If there is more than one person going into the final hour the run will become a foot race to the finish! If you complete all 8 loops, you will have run approximately 32 Miles! Do you have what it takes? Do one loop, 3 loops or all 8! It’s sure to be a good time for the runners and the spectators!

 

After the race head up to Bidwell Golf Course Bar and grill for some delicious food and drinks! All runners get a breakfast burrito with your race registration plus and additional 15% off any other food or drink. 

 

By supporting this race, you are supporting two great causes! 

Chico Velo Trailworks. Launched in 2014, Chico Velo’s Trailworks supports and manages the creation and maintenance of sustainable and enjoyable trails in our region. They have established a strong partnership with the City of Chico to maintain the trails in Upper Bidwell Park. Trailworks have done additional work in the Oroville area and beyond. They are actively seeking new partnerships and opportunities within our community to promote sustainable trail design. Trailworks volunteers put in hundreds of hours every year improving trails for all users to enjoy. To see their latest project check out our Colby Mountain Recreation Project.  A portion of your race entry will go to this great local stewardship as they continue their work to help keep our local trails accessible for us all! If you would like more information on this program or would like to sign up for a park cleanup day, click the link below.

Chico Velo Trailworks - CHICO VELO

 

In addition to supporting Chico Velo Trailworks we are also donating a portion of the race proceeds to local fire academy cadets. Many of the current class are volunteer firefighters who have worked and volunteered in our community and are continuing their education to be able to make a lifelong career the Fire industry. With a fire prone environment that we live in throughout Butte County we rely on our local fire personnel, staff and volunteers to keep our community safe! Cadets will be volunteering on the racecourse to help ensure the safety of all our participants.  Cadets can be seen on our racecourse supporting our race as emergency EMTs and safety aids at the creek crossings. If you are interested in becoming a volunteer firefighter visit the links below for more information.

Become a Volunteer | Butte County, CA

name: Fog Run
description:
The Probation Auxiliary County of Kern presents their 36th Annual 5K-10K Fog Run at Lake Ming in Bakersfield. This is a fun and family friendly 5K-10K race to support at-risk individuals in Kern County.

Proceeds will also benefit the Kern County Probation Department's Helping Hands program. Helping Hands is a nonprofit organization, and their goal is to guide at risk youth towards success by removing barriers and equipping them with the basic needs. Together the two organizations provide scholarships, vocational training, mentoring, clothing, hygiene products, and other necessities.  We believe our programs leave a lasting impact on youth by removing barriers and increasing self-esteem, confidence, and drive to go to school. It is our hope to set up individuals for success and make our community a safer place. The race takes place on a beautiful scenic course overlooking beautiful mountains and lake views.

Packet Pickup

Thursday, January 8, 2026, from 4:30PM – 6:30PM at Kern County Probation Department, 2005 Ridge Rd., Bakersfield, CA 93305
Friday, January 9, 2026, from 4:00PM – 6:00PM at Orangetheory Fitness, 12838 Stockdale Hwy Suites 4A-1 & 4A-2, Bakersfield, CA 93314
Race Day Check-in/Packet Pickup: January 10, 2026, 6:30am – 7:30am at Lake Ming 

 
Event will occur rain or shine.

name: For The Bay 5K Run 2026
description:
Lace Up for a Cause, Support Bay Area Youth

Shoreline Park, Mountain View, CA US 94043

 

"For The Bay 5K" is a fundraiser for Mobilize Love, a Menlo Church ministry partner, providing academic support, mentorship, and life skills training to under-resourced youth in the Bay Area. Mobilize Love's mobile after-school programs and human services address physical needs, develop life skills, and build community, fostering flourishing lives for children and families.

Each increment of $32,000 covers the cost of providing after school services to kids in resource-challenged public schools for the year. These after-school services are characterized by:

  • Introducing and sharing the Gospel
  • Providing nutritious and delicious meals-You can't learn if you're hungry
  • Establishing a consistent presence and trust

 

Visit Mobilize Love to learn more about their incredible impact on our community.

name: Fort Bragg Whale Run and Walk
description:
The 38th Annual Whale Run & Walk for 2026!
Fort Bragg, Ca is a small, picturesque city on the Pacific Ocean, nestled between sandy beaches and the redwood forest. Every year there is a huge Whale Festival on the 2nd weekend of March, and the morning Whale Run kicks it off! After the Whale Run there are events all over town, including a craft fair, guided whale viewing, beer and wine tasting, and a live symphony concert in the evening.

The local Fort Bragg Soroptimists have been holding this race for 38 years, with as many as 800 runners participating on a beautiful day on the Mendocino Coast. The ocean and trails are as magnificent as ever and we know you will love the views and all the festivities in town on race day. All runners, walkers, and spectators will enjoy breathtaking whitewater ocean views (including whales) along this year’s new course starting at the Noyo Headlands Park (Cypress Street) on the Coastal Trail in Fort Bragg, CA

Here are the events you can sign up for:

  • 5k-- runners will run north and turn around at or near Compass Rose.
  • 5k-- "Fun" Walkers will follow the 5k runners route. 
  • 10k-- runners dash north past Glass Beach then cross the beautiful Pudding Creek Trestle to the 10K turn around (10K map).
  • 1/2 Marathon--same route as 10k but the turnaround is at MacKerricher State Park.
  • Kiddie run -- 300 meter run in 2 age groups (U6 and U10)

There are multiple race age divisions. Note: under 16 run/walkers may enter any race division for a discounted rate at signup.

Early signups are encouraged!! The entry fee will increase starting March 1, 2025. We also have some inventory of last year's tshirts for sale for $10 plus shipping: go to https://runsignup.com/Race/Store/CA/FortBragg/FortBraggWhaleRunandWalk 

DOGS: We may actually have a dog entry option!!  Details soon.

name: Foster the Future Run
description:
The 9th Annual Foster The Future 5/10K Run/Walk Beyond Foster Care Wellness Fest is coming to Pasadena, California just north of the world famous Rose Bowl! Join us for this is a wonderful wellness opportunity to help support Journey House, Pasadena; providing services for former foster youth since 1983.

Journey House's Mission is to support former foster and probation youth to live fully independent, successful lives.
Founded in 1983, Journey House provides emotional support and guidance, as well as financial aid to help them with the cost of attending college and vocational schools.
Our goal is to create opportunities for advancement in education, economic stability, and a better quality of life for former foster youth.

For more information visit: journeyhouseyouth.org

name: Foster5K + Kids Dash
description:
The 9th Annual Foster5K + Kids Dash

Sunday, April 27, 2025

The Foster5k is a cornerstone event in Silicon Valley dedicated to championing the cause of foster children in Santa Clara County. All proceeds support Child Advocates of Silicon Valley (CASV) and its Court Appointed Special Advocate (CASA) Program, dedicated to providing everlasting impact on our community's most vulnerable youth.
The Foster5K features a chip-timed race and a Kids Dash, making the event enjoyable for walkers, joggers, and runners of all ages. The Kids Dash is a fun-filled event designed just for kids! This untimed fun run features a 700 meter Big Kids Dash for youth ages 6 to 10 and a 250 meter Little Kids Dash for children ages 5 and under. The Kids Dash focuses on fun, movement, and participation.
Whether sprinting, jogging, or skipping to the finish line, everyone can have a good time and support our community's foster youth along the way. See you there!

 

All proceeds benefit Child Advocates of Silicon Valley, an independent nonprofit serving our community's most vulnerable youth - foster children aged birth to 21 years old who have experienced abuse, neglect and/or abandonment. Together we can help LIFT UP our foster children. Learn more about how to help a child in foster care at childadvocatessv.org.

name: Freedom Run
description: Welcome to the Fresno Freedom Run! Start off your 4th of July celebrations with a bang and beautiful 4-mile run! The event will take place at Woodward Park with hundreds of acres of trees, geese, and beautiful wildlife. We are sure it will be an adventure! You will enjoy our American flag lined course. We hope to inspire you to race, run or walk at the best of your ability. Motivate your friends, family and fellow competitors to join in. What a way to start one of the most important days of the year for our great country.

name: FRESNO 5,000M
description:
Experience the thrill of a true track event! The 5,000M run, often referred to as a "5K on the track," challenges athletes to complete 12.5 laps on a standard track. This event is perfect for both seasoned runners and those looking to try a track race for the first time—or for the first time in a long time!

 

This isn’t just a race—it’s a chance to support the Fresno High School Track Team, with 100% of proceeds going directly to the program. And the fun doesn’t stop with the 5,000M! We also offer an Open Mile Run and a 100-Meter Kids Race, plus a spirited 4x400M Relay to close out the event.

 

Whether you're chasing a personal best or simply enjoying the camaraderie of the running community, this event has something for everyone!

name: Fresno Turkey Trot
description:
Sierra Challenge Express

Presents:

the 27th annual

Fresno Turkey Trot @ Woodward Park

 

For over a quarter of a century, the Fresno running community has come together on Thanksgiving morning to make a difference — supporting the hungry in our city through generous donations and race registrations. The Fresno Turkey Trot isn’t just a run; it’s a tradition of gratitude, generosity, and good times. This year, your participation not only benefits the Central California Food Bank, but also supports the Coach Ray Knight Youth and Scholarship Programs, helping student-athletes across the Central Valley pursue their academic and athletic dreams.

Kick off your Thanksgiving with purpose! Whether you run the chip-timed 5K or enjoy the untimed 2-Mile Walk, you’ll be part of a festive and meaningful morning. Every participant will receive a long-sleeve Thanksgiving shirt, a commemorative finisher’s medal, and a tasty post-race treat.

name: Fresno Urban Run
description:
The 2026 date for the Fresno Urban run is still pending.  We will open as soon as we have a confirmed date!

 

Starting inside of Chukchansi Park, you will be put to the challenge of climbing every step from the bottom to the top of the stadium, followed by a run up a 6-story circular garage and then down an adjacent 6-story circular garage, proceeded by a half-mile run down Fulton Street to the Tuolumne Overpass (Urban Hill), before the final challenge, climbing 220 stairs to the top of a 10-story building, The Grand Tower, where your timing sensor will stop your clock!
Overall length of the Urban Run is approx 3 Miles.  
All donations support The Alisa Ann Ruch Burn Foundation!

The Fresno Urban Run is a 20 point race in the California Classic Runner of the Year Series!

name: Friday the 13th -Camp Heartbreak  -After Dark  5K. 10K Half Marathon  by Califlow Runs
description:
💔 Camp Heartbreak – Run If You Dare
🌙 Friday the 13th of February – Long Beach
5K | 10K | Half Marathon
📍 5400 E. Ocean Blvd, Long Beach, CA
📅 Friday, February 13, 2026
🕓 Check-in 4:00 PM
Start Times (Based on distance) | Half 5:00 PM | 10K & 5K 6:30 PM

 
💘 About the Event
Welcome to Camp Heartbreak, where love stories end in sprint finishes and Cupid’s arrows miss… on purpose. 💀


They say heartbreak hurts — but here, it burns calories.

Join us for Run If You Dare, a Friday-the-13th Valentine’s race that mixes romance and ruin under the moonlit shoreline of Long Beach. Whether you’re running from your ex, chasing closure, or just here for the medal and the music, this night’s for the fearless and the heart-strong.

 
🌊 What to Expect
USATF-Certified Course 🏁
Professional Chip Timing ⏱️
Free Race-Day Photos 📸
Finisher Medals for All Participants 🏅
Overall & Age Group Awards
3 On-Course Water Stations (one at each turnaround)
Finish-Line Festival & Camp Dance Party 🎶
Costume Contest — Best Heartbreaker & Most Tragic Love Story 👠💔
DJ, Lights & Glow Effects for that classic CaliFlow After-Dark vibe
Runners, Walkers & Lovelorn Souls of All Paces Welcome!
 
🩶 Course Info
Your journey begins beneath the glowing CaliFlow arch at 5400 E. Ocean Blvd, tracing a flat, paved path along the waves — scenic, fast, and a little bit sinister.

Each turnaround hides a “Camp Heartbreak” surprise — maybe a runaway Cupid, a rose-covered machete, or a love letter gone wrong.

Half Marathon: 3 × 4.36-mile loops
10K: 2 × 5K out-and-backs
5K: 1 loop

Every station features glowing course markers, cheering “counselors,” and enough good vibes to heal even the most tragic of love lives.

 
🔥 The Vibe – Totally Camp CaliFlow


Think Valentine’s Day Massacre meets Glow Run Rom-Com.
We’re talking camp signs, flickering lanterns, red lights, and finish-line slow jams.

Whether you come solo, with your sweetheart, or as a crew of heartbreak survivors, one thing’s for sure — you’ll leave with a full heart and maybe a few goosebumps.

Because at CaliFlow Runs, we don’t fear Friday the 13th.
We run right through it — in style, with heart, and with a whole lot of glow.

✨ Not just a race. Join the movement.
